text:
1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND APPLICABILITY
1.1 Purpose. This Policy sets out the types of leave available to Employees of the Company, the entitlement to each type of leave, the manner of accrual, carry-forward and encashment, and the procedure for applying for and sanctioning leave. It is intended to allow Employees adequate rest and time for personal and family needs while ensuring continuity of service to the Company's clients.
1.2 Scope. This Policy applies to every Employee in Grades L1 to L8 working at the Company's offices in Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai and Noida, and to Employees working from home or at a client location in India. It does not apply to: (a) consultants, retainers and persons engaged through a manpower agency, whose leave is governed by their contract; (b) interns and apprentices, whose leave is governed by their letter of engagement; and (c) Employees on an international assignment, whose leave is governed by the assignment letter and the law of the host country, save that Earned Leave continues to accrue under this Policy.

2. DEFINITIONS
In this Policy, unless the context otherwise requires, the following terms have the meanings given below. Words in the singular include the plural and vice versa.
2.1 "Basic Salary" means the monthly basic pay of an Employee as stated in the Employee's current compensation letter, excluding all allowances, variable pay, reimbursements and perquisites.
2.2 "Calendar Day" means any day of the year, including weekly offs and holidays.
2.3 "Company" means Nexora Technologies Limited and includes its offices and delivery centres in India.
2.4 "Confirmed Employee" means an Employee whose probation has been completed and who has received a written confirmation of service through the NPP.
2.5 "Continuous Service" means uninterrupted service with the Company, including periods of paid leave, maternity leave and authorised absence, but excluding any period of Leave Without Pay exceeding 30 Calendar Days in aggregate in a Leave Year and any period of unauthorised absence.

text:
3. GENERAL PRINCIPLES
3.1 Leave is not a matter of right. Leave cannot be claimed as a matter of right. Sanction of leave is subject to the exigencies of work, and the Reporting Manager may refuse, defer or curtail leave, recording the reason on the NPP. Leave shall not ordinarily be refused where the Employee would otherwise lose a balance that lapses at the end of the Leave Year.
3.2 Credit of leave. Casual Leave and Sick Leave are credited in full on 1 April of each Leave Year. Earned Leave is credited monthly, in advance, on the first day of each month at one-twelfth of the annual entitlement in Table 1.
3.3 Proration for joiners. An Employee who joins on or before the 15th day of a month receives the Earned Leave credit for that month; an Employee who joins after the 15th day receives credit from the following month. Casual Leave and Sick Leave for the joining year are prorated for the number of months remaining in the Leave Year, including the month of joining, and rounded to the nearest half day.

3.4 Sandwich rule. Where a single spell of Earned Leave covers five or more Working Days, weekly offs and holidays falling within that spell are counted as Earned Leave. Where the spell covers fewer than five Working Days, intervening weekly offs and holidays are not counted. The sandwich rule does not apply to Casual Leave, Sick Leave or any leave under Section 6.
3.5 Combination of leave. Earned Leave may be combined with Sick Leave and with any leave under Section 6. Casual Leave shall not be combined with Earned Leave or Sick Leave, whether by prefixing or suffixing, as provided in Clause 5.2.

title: Leave Policy
text:
4. EARNED LEAVE
4.1 Entitlement. Earned Leave (EL) is intended for planned rest and recreation. The annual entitlement of EL, and of Casual Leave and Sick Leave, together with the accumulation limit and encashment eligibility for each Grade, is set out in Table 1.
Sick Leave may be accumulated up to 24 days in all Grades. Casual Leave lapses on 31 March and is not carried forward. An Employee promoted during a Leave Year receives the EL entitlement of the new Grade from the month following the effective date of promotion.
4.2 Advance application. EL of up to three Working Days shall be applied for on the NPP at least three Working Days in advance. EL of more than three Working Days shall be applied for at least 14 Calendar Days in advance, so that project staffing can be adjusted. EL taken without advance application, other than in an emergency accepted by the Reporting Manager, may be treated as Leave Without Pay.

text:
4.3 Accumulation and carry-forward. Unused EL is carried forward to the next Leave Year up to the accumulation limit for the Employee's Grade in Table 1.
4.3.1 EL in excess of the accumulation limit on 31 March lapses automatically and is neither carried forward nor encashed.
4.3.2 The NPP notifies each Employee in February of any balance projected to lapse, so that the Employee may plan leave before 31 March.
4.3.3 An Employee in Grades L6 to L8 who holds a role designated as sensitive by the Finance or Internal Audit function shall take at least five consecutive Working Days of EL in each Leave Year.
4.4 Encashment during service. Encashment of EL during service is available only to Employees in Grades L3 to L8, up to the number of days stated for the Grade in Table 1. Employees in Grades L1 and L2 are not eligible for encashment during service. Encashment is subject to the following conditions: (a) the Employee is a Confirmed Employee on the date of application; (b) the EL balance remaining after encashment is not less than 15 days; (c) the application is made on the NPP between 1 April and 30 April, and payment is made with the salary for May; and (d) encashment is calculated at Basic Salary divided by 26 for each day encashed, and is taxable as salary.
4.5 Advance Earned Leave. A Confirmed Employee who has exhausted EL may, with the approval of the HR Business Partner, be granted up to five days of EL in advance of accrual. Any advance not recovered by subsequent accrual is recovered in the full and final settlement under Clause 11.3.

title: Leave Policy
text:
5. CASUAL LEAVE AND SICK LEAVE
5.1 Casual Leave. Casual Leave (CL) is intended for unforeseen personal needs. Not more than three days of CL may be taken at a time. CL is not encashed and lapses on 31 March.
5.2 No combination with Earned Leave. CL shall not be prefixed or suffixed to EL or Sick Leave. Where an Employee applies for CL immediately before or after EL, the entire spell shall be treated as EL and debited accordingly.
5.3 Sick Leave. Sick Leave (SL) is available for the Employee's own illness or injury. Unused SL is carried forward up to a maximum of 24 days and is not encashed at any time.

5.3 Sick Leave. Sick Leave (SL) is available for the Employee's own illness or injury. Unused SL is carried forward up to a maximum of 24 days and is not encashed at any time.

title: Leave Policy
text:
5.4 Medical certificate. SL of more than two consecutive Working Days shall be supported by a certificate from a registered medical practitioner, uploaded on the NPP within three Working Days of resuming duty. SL of more than seven consecutive Calendar Days shall additionally be supported by a certificate of fitness to resume duty.
5.5 Exhaustion of Sick Leave. Where SL is exhausted, the absence is debited to EL and thereafter treated as Leave Without Pay. CL shall not be used to cover sickness beyond three days.
5.6 Special sick leave for hospitalisation. A Confirmed Employee who is hospitalised for more than seven consecutive Calendar Days and has exhausted SL may be granted special sick leave on full pay of up to 30 Calendar Days, once during service, on the recommendation of the HR Business Partner and the approval of the Head, HR Operations. Hospital discharge papers shall be submitted.

6. MATERNITY, ADOPTION AND PATERNITY LEAVE
6.1 General. Leave under this Section is in addition to the leave in Table 1, is not debited from any leave balance and is not subject to the sandwich rule. Maternity leave is paid at full salary, comprising Basic Salary and all fixed allowances; an Employee covered by the Employees' State Insurance scheme receives the maternity benefit from the ESI Corporation, and the Company pays only the difference, if any.
6.2 Maternity leave.
6.2.1 A woman Employee who has actually worked for the Company for not less than eighty days in the twelve months immediately preceding her expected date of delivery is entitled to maternity leave.
6.2.2 Maternity leave is 26 weeks, of which not more than eight weeks may precede the expected date of delivery. For a woman Employee who has two or more surviving children, maternity leave is 12 weeks, of which not more than six weeks may precede the expected date of delivery.

8. LEAVE WITHOUT PAY AND SABBATICAL
8.1 Leave Without Pay. Leave Without Pay may be sanctioned only where the Employee has no balance of the relevant leave. LWP of up to 30 Calendar Days in a Leave Year may be approved by the Reporting Manager and the HR Business Partner; LWP beyond 30 Calendar Days requires the approval of the Chief People Officer.
8.1.1 No EL accrues for any month in which the Employee is on LWP for more than ten Calendar Days.
8.1.2 LWP exceeding 30 Calendar Days in aggregate in a Leave Year does not count as Continuous Service.
8.2 Unauthorised absence. Absence without sanctioned leave is treated as LWP and may lead to disciplinary action under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004). Absence without intimation for eight or more consecutive Working Days is dealt with under the absconding procedure in the Separation and Exit Policy (NTL/HR/POL/008).

9. HOLIDAYS
9.1 Declared and restricted holidays. Each location observes ten declared holidays in a calendar year, as listed in Annexure B. In addition, each Employee may choose two restricted holidays from the list in Annexure B, applied for on the NPP at least seven Calendar Days in advance.
9.2 Holiday calendar. The holiday calendar follows the calendar year from January to December and is published on the NPP by 15 December of the preceding year, with the dates of festivals notified for each location. The holiday calendar therefore does not coincide with the Leave Year.
9.3 Base location. Holidays follow the Employee's base location recorded on the NPP and not the location of a client. An Employee deputed to a client site in another city for more than 30 Calendar Days may, with the approval of the HR Business Partner, follow the holiday calendar of the client location instead.
9.4 Work on a holiday. Work on a declared holiday requires prior approval of the Reporting Manager and is compensated under Clause 7.3.
9.5 State legislation. The minimum number of national and festival holidays, and certain leave conditions, are prescribed by the law of each State. The legislation applicable to each location is listed in Table 2. Where the State law prescribes a higher benefit than this Policy, Clause 1.5 applies.

10. APPLICATION, APPROVAL AND RECORDS
10.1 Application through the NPP. All leave shall be applied for, approved and cancelled on the NPP. The manual form in Annexure A may be used only where the NPP is unavailable for more than one Working Day or the Employee has no system access, and shall be regularised on the NPP within five Working Days of the NPP becoming available.
10.2 Approval matrix. Leave is approved by the authorities, and within the turnaround times, set out in Table 3.
10.3 No deemed approval. An application not acted upon within the turnaround time is escalated automatically by the NPP to the next approver in Table 3. Leave is never deemed to be approved by lapse of time, and an Employee shall not proceed on leave without an approval recorded on the NPP, except in an emergency.
10.4 Recall from leave. In an exigency, the Company may recall an Employee from sanctioned EL. The unavailed portion of the leave is re-credited, and the cost of return travel and any non-refundable booking is reimbursed under the Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy (NTL/HR/POL/007).
10.5 Leave records. Leave balances are visible to each Employee on the NPP. An Employee who believes a balance is incorrect shall raise a ticket in the Leave category through the HR Helpdesk within 30 Calendar Days of the credit or debit concerned. Unresolved concerns are escalated as set out in Annexure C.

section_title: Leave During Notice Period and on Separation
text:
11. LEAVE DURING NOTICE PERIOD AND ON SEPARATION
11.1 Leave during the notice period. An Employee serving notice may not avail EL except with the approval of the Reporting Manager and the HR Business Partner. SL supported by a medical certificate may be availed. Any leave other than such SL that is availed during the notice period extends the last day of service by the number of days of leave, unless the Reporting Manager waives the extension in writing.
11.2 Encashment on separation. On separation for any reason other than death, the EL balance on the last day of service is encashed up to the accumulation limit for the Employee's Grade in Table 1, at Basic Salary divided by 26 for each day. CL and SL are not encashed. The encashment is paid with the full and final settlement.

12.1 Responsibility. HR Operations administers this Policy and maintains leave records. Reporting Managers are responsible for timely decisions on applications and for planning team leave so that no Employee is prevented from availing leave that would otherwise lapse.
12.2 Misuse. Submission of a false medical certificate or document, or misrepresentation of the purpose of leave, is misconduct and shall be dealt with under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).
12.3 Review. This Policy is reviewed annually by HR Operations and on any change in applicable law. Suggestions may be sent to the HR Helpdesk.
12.4 Confidentiality of medical and personal documents. Medical certificates, discharge summaries, pregnancy certificates and adoption orders submitted under this Policy are personal data. They are stored in a restricted section of the NPP that is accessible only to HR Operations and the HR Business Partner, are not visible to the Reporting Manager, and are retained and deleted in accordance with the IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy (NTL/HR/POL/009). The Reporting Manager sees only the type and dates of leave.

ANNEXURE C: ESCALATION MATRIX FOR LEAVE CONCERNS
An Employee who is dissatisfied with a decision on leave, or with the correction of a leave balance, may escalate the matter in the following order. Each level shall respond within the stated time; if it does not, the Employee may proceed to the next level.
Table 5: Escalation levels for leave concerns
Level: 1 | Escalate to: HR Helpdesk | How: Ticket in the Leave category on the NPP, or hrhelpdesk@nexora.example | Response time: 3 Working Days
Level: 2 | Escalate to: HR Business Partner | How: Reply to the ticket requesting escalation | Response time: 3 Working Days
Level: 3 | Escalate to: Head, HR Operations | How: E-mail with the ticket number | Response time: 5 Working Days
Level: 4 | Escalate to: Chief People Officer | How: E-mail with the ticket number and previous responses | Response time: 10 Working Days
Concerns involving harassment, discrimination or retaliation connected with leave, for example refusal of leave linked to pregnancy, shall not follow this matrix. They are raised under the Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) (NTL/HR/POL/003) or the whistleblower mechanism in the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).

ANNEXURE D: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS AND ILLUSTRATIONS
The answers below illustrate the application of this Policy. Where an answer and a clause of the Policy appear to differ, the clause prevails, save that the carve-out in Clause D.6 forms part of this Policy.
D.1 How is the sandwich rule applied? An Employee takes EL from Thursday to the following Tuesday. The spell covers four Working Days (Thursday, Friday, Monday and Tuesday), which is fewer than five, so the intervening Saturday and Sunday are not counted and four days of EL are debited. If the same Employee takes EL from Thursday to the following Wednesday, the spell covers five Working Days, so the Saturday and Sunday are counted and seven days of EL are debited under Clause 3.4.

D.1 How is the sandwich rule applied? An Employee takes EL from Thursday to the following Tuesday. The spell covers four Working Days (Thursday, Friday, Monday and Tuesday), which is fewer than five, so the intervening Saturday and Sunday are not counted and four days of EL are debited. title: Leave Policy
text:
D.2 How is leave prorated for a new joiner? An Employee in Grade L3 joins on 10 August. Having joined on or before the 15th, the Employee receives EL credit from August: eight months at 1.5 days a month, or 12 days by 31 March. CL is prorated as 7 multiplied by 8/12, or 4.67 days, rounded to 4.5 days; SL is prorated as 8 multiplied by 8/12, or 5.33 days, rounded to 5.5 days.
D.3 How is EL encashed on separation? An Employee in Grade L5 with a Basic Salary of Rs. 60,000 a month resigns with an EL balance of 52 days. The accumulation limit for L5 is 45 days, so 45 days are encashed: Rs. 60,000 divided by 26, multiplied by 45, which is Rs. 1,03,846. The remaining seven days lapse.

text:
D.4 Can I take bereavement leave on the death of a grandparent or parent-in-law? No. Bereavement leave under Clause 7.1 applies only to the Immediate Family as defined in Clause 2.8, which does not include grandparents or parents-in-law. CL or EL may be used instead, and the Reporting Manager is expected to approve it at short notice.
D.5 My team works on Saturdays for a client. Do Saturdays count as Working Days for my leave? No. Under Clause 2.14, Saturdays and Sundays are never Working Days for the purposes of this Policy, even under a client roster. Work on a Saturday may qualify for compensatory off under Clause 7.3 if the Employee is in Grades L1 to L4.

title: Leave Policy
text:
D.6 Can an Employee in Grade L4 take a sabbatical? Ordinarily no, because Clause 8.3 limits sabbatical to Grade L5 and above. However, an Employee in Grade L4 with at least five years of Continuous Service who has been admitted to a full-time postgraduate programme sponsored by the Company may be granted a sabbatical of up to six months with the approval of the Business Unit Head and the Chief People Officer. This carve-out does not extend to Grades L1 to L3.
D.7 Can I encash EL during service if I am in Grade L2? No. Encashment during service is available only in Grades L3 to L8 under Clause 4.4. An Employee in Grade L2 may carry forward EL up to 45 days, and the balance within that limit is encashed on separation under Clause 11.2.

Date of Issue: 2025-06-20
Effective From: 2025-07-01
Subject: Enhancement of paternity leave
Amends: Clause 6.4.1, Clause 6.4.2
Issued By: Chief People Officer
With effect from 1 July 2025, paternity leave under Clause 6.4.1 is increased from 5 Working Days to 10 Working Days, to be availed within six months of the date of birth or adoption. The limit of two children during service continues to apply. Notwithstanding Clause 6.4.2, paternity leave may be taken in up to two spells within the six-month period. (a) This Circular applies where the date of birth or adoption is on or after 1 July 2025. Where the date of birth or adoption is before 1 July 2025, the entitlement remains 5 Working Days within three months. (b) All other provisions of the Policy remain unchanged. This Circular prevails over the body of the Policy to the extent of any inconsistency.

text:
CIRCULAR NO. HR/CIR/2025/11
Circular No.: HR/CIR/2025/11
Date of Issue: 2025-09-12
Effective From: 2025-10-01
Subject: Combination of Casual Leave with Earned Leave
Amends: Clause 3.5, Clause 5.2
Issued By: Chief People Officer
With effect from 1 October 2025, Casual Leave may be prefixed or suffixed to Earned Leave, provided that the combined spell does not exceed 10 Working Days. The CL portion is debited to CL and the EL portion to EL, and the sandwich rule in Clause 3.4 is applied to the combined spell as if it were a spell of EL. CL still may not be combined with Sick Leave. Clause 3.5 and Clause 5.2 stand amended accordingly.

Amends: Clause 3.5, Clause 5.2
Issued By: Chief People Officer
With effect from 1 October 2025, Casual Leave may be prefixed or suffixed to Earned Leave, provided that the combined spell does not exceed 10 Working Days. The CL portion is debited to CL and the EL portion to EL, and the sandwich rule in Clause 3.4 is applied to the combined spell as if it were a spell of EL. CL still may not be combined with Sick Leave. Clause 3.5 and Clause 5.2 stand amended accordingly.

title: Employee Handbook
text:
1. ABOUT THIS HANDBOOK
1.1 Purpose. This Handbook introduces Employees to the Company, explains how the Company works day to day, and summarises the principal policies that govern employment. It is written to be read in full by every new Employee during the first week and to serve thereafter as a quick reference.
1.2 Status of this Handbook. This Handbook is a summary. It does not form part of any contract of employment and does not create any right that is not provided in the policy on which a summary is based. Each summary names the governing policy, which should be consulted for the complete rule, its conditions and its exceptions.
1.3 Policy hierarchy. Where two documents appear to give different answers on the same matter, the following order of precedence applies: (a) applicable law, including any statute, rule or notification, prevails over any policy of the Company that provides a lesser benefit or a contrary rule; (b) an amendment circular in the HR/CIR series prevails, from its effective date, over the clause of the policy that it amends; (c) the specific policy on a subject prevails over this Handbook, which is only a summary; and (d) between two policies, the policy that governs the subject matter prevails, for example the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001) on leave and leave encashment, and the Separation and Exit Policy (NTL/HR/POL/008) on notice periods.
1.4 Circulars and updates. Policies change during the year through amendment circulars, which are published on the NPP and announced by e-mail. This Handbook is re-issued once a year and may therefore not reflect a circular issued after its effective date. Employees should check the circulars at the end of the governing policy before acting on a summary in this Handbook.
1.5 Questions. Questions about this Handbook or any policy may be raised with the HR Business Partner or as a ticket through the HR Helpdesk. An answer given by the HR Helpdesk is guidance on the policy and does not change it.

3. ABOUT NEXORA
3.1 Who we are. The Company was incorporated in Bengaluru in 2009 as a software services firm and today employs about 18,000 people across five delivery centres in India. It provides application development, application maintenance, cloud migration, data engineering and testing services to clients in banking, insurance, healthcare, retail and manufacturing, principally in India, the United Kingdom and North America.
3.2 Business units. Delivery is organised into five business units: Banking and Financial Services; Healthcare and Life Sciences; Retail and Consumer; Digital Engineering; and Cloud and Infrastructure Services. Corporate functions, including HR, Finance, Legal, Information Security, Facilities and the Travel Desk, support all business units from Bengaluru, with local teams at each location.

title: Employee Handbook
text:
4. JOINING AND PROBATION
4.1 Joining formalities. On the date of joining, a new Employee completes the joining formalities on the NPP, submits the documents listed in Annexure B, and receives an identity card, a laptop and system access. Original documents are verified and returned on the same day; the Company does not retain original certificates.
4.2 Background verification. Every offer is subject to background verification of identity, address, education, previous employment and, where permitted by law, criminal records, carried out by an authorised third-party agency with the Employee's written consent. Verification is ordinarily completed within 60 days of joining. A material discrepancy, such as a false degree or concealed employment, may result in withdrawal of the offer or termination of employment in accordance with the Separation and Exit Policy
(NTL/HR/POL/008).

text:
4.3 Induction. All new Employees attend the Nexora Foundation Programme, a five-day induction covering the Company's business, values, policies, information security and the POSH policy. Completion of the induction modules on the NPP, including the information security and POSH assessments, is mandatory within 30 days of joining.
4.4 Graduate trainees. Employees joining in Grade L1 as Graduate Engineer Trainees complete a twelve-week technical programme at the Learning Academy in Bengaluru or Hyderabad before deployment to a project. 5. WORKING HOURS, ATTENDANCE AND HYBRID WORK
Governing policy: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy (NTL/HR/POL/006). The summary below reflects that policy as on 1 April 2025.
5.1 Working week. The standard working week is Monday to Friday. A working day is nine hours, including a one-hour meal break, and the Company expects about 45 hours of presence a week. Core hours, during which Employees are expected to be available for meetings, are 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. in the Employee's time zone.
5.2 Attendance recording. Attendance is recorded by the identity card at office entry points and, on days of remote work, by marking attendance on the NPP. Missed or incorrect punches may be regularised on the NPP, with the approval of the Reporting Manager, up to three times in a calendar month.

title: Employee Handbook
text:
6. LEAVE AND HOLIDAYS
Governing policy: Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001). In any inconsistency the Leave Policy and its circulars prevail.
6.1 Annual leave at a glance. Leave is credited for the Leave Year from 1 April to 31 March. The principal entitlements are summarised in Table 3; conditions such as advance notice, the sandwich rule and accumulation limits are in the Leave Policy.
6.2 Family-related leave. A woman Employee who meets the eligibility conditions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 receives 26 weeks of paid maternity leave, and 12 weeks on adoption of a child below three months. A male Employee receives paternity leave of 5 Working Days, to be taken within three months of the birth or adoption of a child, for up to two children. Bereavement leave of 3 Working Days is available on the death of an Immediate Family member, and marriage leave of 3 Working Days once during service.
6.3 Holidays. Each location observes ten declared holidays in a calendar year, and each Employee may choose two restricted holidays. The holiday calendar for each location is published on the NPP in December for the following calendar year.

Governing policy for insurance and retirement benefits: Compensation and Benefits Policy (NTL/HR/POL/005). Creche and day-care arrangements are governed by this Handbook.
8.1 Insurance. Every Employee is covered from the date of joining by group medical insurance for the Employee, spouse and up to two children, by group personal accident insurance and by group term life insurance. 9. PERFORMANCE AND CAREER GROWTH
9.1 Performance cycle. The performance year runs from 1 April to 31 March. Goals are agreed on the NPP by 30 April, reviewed at a mid-year check-in in October, and assessed in the annual review in April and May. Employees who joined after 31 December are not rated for that year and are reviewed in the following cycle.
9.2 Ratings. Performance is rated on the five-point scale in Table 5. Ratings proposed by Reporting Managers are reviewed in a normalisation meeting within each business unit to ensure consistent standards. The Employee sees the final rating and the manager's comments on the NPP and may request a discussion with the skip-level manager within 15 days.
9.3 Promotions. Promotions are decided once a year, effective 1 July, on the basis of performance, demonstrated capability at the next Grade and business need. The minimum time in Grade before promotion is 12 months from L1 to L2, 24 months for promotion from L2, L3 and L4, and 36 months for promotion from L5 and above. A rating of 4 or 5 in the most recent cycle is ordinarily expected.

10. LEARNING AND DEVELOPMENT
10.1 Learning hours. Every Employee is expected to complete at least 40 hours of learning in a performance year through the Learning Academy, the online library on the NPP, or approved external programmes. Mandatory compliance modules count towards these hours.
10.2 Certification reimbursement. An Employee in Grade L3 or above who passes a certification approved for the Employee's role may claim reimbursement of the examination fee, up to Rs. 50,000 in a performance year. An Employee who resigns within 12 months of the reimbursement repays it in full through the full and final settlement. Employees in Grades L1 and L2 are nominated for certifications by the Learning Academy, which pays the fee directly and does not require repayment.
10.3 Higher education. The Company may sponsor a part-time postgraduate programme for a Confirmed Employee with at least three years of service, meeting up to 75 per cent of the fees subject to a service agreement of 24 months after completion. Full-time programmes may be supported by a sabbatical under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001).
10.4 Mentoring. Every Employee in Grades L1 and L2 is assigned a mentor from Grade L4 or above for the first year. Mentors meet mentees at least once a month; the mentoring relationship is separate from the reporting line.

A complaint is made in writing to the Internal Committee at ic@nexora.example. The process, timelines and protections are in the Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) (NTL/HR/POL/003); Employees should read that policy rather than rely on this summary.
13.2 Grievances. Any other work-related grievance, such as a concern about allocation of work, a manager's conduct, or the application of a policy, is first raised with the Reporting Manager or the HR Business Partner. If it is not resolved within ten Working Days, the Employee may raise it in writing with the location Grievance Committee, chaired by a senior leader, which responds within 15 Working Days.
13.3 Ethics concerns. Concerns about fraud, bribery, conflicts of interest, data misuse or any breach of law may be raised with the Ethics Office at ethics@nexora.example or through the ethics hotline at 1800-000-0000 (extension 7), anonymously if the Employee prefers.
13.4 No retaliation. No Employee shall suffer any adverse consequence for raising a grievance, a complaint or an ethics concern in good faith, or for participating in an inquiry as a witness. Retaliation is itself misconduct.

14. INFORMATION SECURITY ESSENTIALS
Governing policy: IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy (NTL/HR/POL/009).
14.1 Your responsibilities. Every Employee protects the information of the Company and its clients. In practice this means: locking the screen when leaving the desk; never sharing passwords or one-time codes; using only Company-approved software and cloud services; never copying client data to a personal device, personal e-mail or unapproved storage; and completing the annual security training.
14.2 Working remotely. When working from home, Employees use the Company laptop and the virtual private network, work where screens cannot be overlooked, and do not print client documents at home. Public Wi-Fi is acceptable only when the virtual private network is switched on.
14.3 Reporting incidents. A lost laptop or phone, a suspicious e-mail, or any suspected disclosure of data is reported immediately to the IT Service Desk at itsd@nexora.example. Early reporting limits harm and is never penalised; concealing an incident is misconduct.

16. HEALTH, SAFETY AND EMERGENCIES
16.1 Safe workplace. The Company maintains its offices in accordance with fire, building and health regulations. Fire drills are held at every location at least twice a year, and each floor has trained fire wardens and first-aid responders whose names are displayed near the lifts.

17. LEAVING THE COMPANY
Governing policy: Separation and Exit Policy (NTL/HR/POL/008). In any inconsistency the Separation and Exit Policy prevails.
17.1 Resignation and notice. An Employee resigns through the NPP. The notice period depends on Grade and is summarised in Table 7. The Reporting Manager may discuss the reasons for resignation, and the Company may, at its discretion, waive part of the notice period.
17.2 Exit process. Before the last day of service the Employee hands over work, returns the laptop, identity card and other Company assets, and obtains clearances on the NPP from the Reporting Manager, IT, Facilities, Finance and HR. An exit interview is offered by the HR Business Partner and its content is kept confidential.
17.3 Full and final settlement and documents. The full and final settlement includes salary for the days worked, leave encashment under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001), gratuity where eligible, and recoveries such as unserved notice or outstanding advances. The relieving letter and service certificate are issued after clearances are complete.

An Employee may be transferred to another location of the Company at the Company's request, for business reasons, or at the Employee's request, subject to a suitable open position. The one-time relocation allowance by Grade is set out in Table 10; it covers packing, transport of household goods and incidental expenses, and is not subject to production of bills.

20.1 Working at a client site. An Employee deployed at a client's premises remains an Employee of the Company and continues to be governed by the Company's policies. 20.3 Complaints at a client site. 23. WORKPLACE FACILITIES AND SERVICES
23.1 Seating. Offices follow a mix of assigned and bookable seating. Employees on hybrid schedules book a desk on the NPP up to 14 days in advance; bookings not checked in by 11:00 a.m. are released. Project areas with client-mandated access controls have assigned seating only.
23.2 Cafeteria and meals. Each location has a cafeteria run by an external caterer, offering subsidised meals during the day and on night shifts. Complaints about food quality are raised through the Facilities module of the NPP and reviewed monthly by a committee that includes Employee representatives.
23.3 Parking. Two-wheeler parking is available to all Employees at every location. Car parking is limited and allocated first to Employees with disabilities, expecting mothers and Employees on night shifts, then by a quarterly draw on the NPP.
23.4 Lactation and quiet rooms. Every location has at least one lactation room and one quiet room. The lactation room may be booked on the NPP or used without booking when free.
23.5 Lost and found. Items found on Company premises are handed to the security desk and recorded. Unclaimed items are kept for 60 days; laptops, phones and identity cards found are handed to the IT Service Desk the same day.

24. REMOTE WORK SUPPORT
24.1 Home office set-up. An Employee approved for hybrid work may claim a one-time home office allowance of up to Rs. 5,000 against bills for an ergonomic chair, a keyboard, a mouse or a monitor stand, within six months of the approval. Items purchased remain the Employee's property. A second claim may be made after 36 months.
24.2 Internet reimbursement. Employees in Grades L1 to L4 on hybrid work may claim reimbursement of home internet charges of up to Rs. 1,000 a month against the bill. Employees in Grades L5 to L8 receive a communication allowance as part of fixed pay and do not claim internet reimbursement separately.
24.3 Working from another city. An Employee may work remotely from a city other than the Base Location for up to 30 Calendar Days in a calendar year, with the Reporting Manager's approval recorded on the NPP. Remote work from outside India is not permitted without the approval of the Chief People Officer and the Head of Information Security, because of tax, immigration and data transfer risks.
24.4 Health and safety at home. Employees working from home are asked to follow the ergonomic guidance on the NPP, take regular breaks, and report any injury sustained while working in the same way as an injury at the office.

25. BUSINESS CONTINUITY AND CRISIS SUPPORT
25.1 When a crisis affects a location. In a flood, epidemic, civil disturbance or similar event, the location Crisis Management Team decides whether the office remains open, and communicates the decision by SMS and e-mail by 6:00 a.m. on the affected day. Employees who cannot reach the office and cannot work from home are covered by the special leave provision of the Leave Policy for calamities.
25.2 Staying reachable. Every Employee keeps an up-to-date personal mobile number and emergency contact on the NPP. During a declared crisis the Company may send safety check messages, and Employees are asked to respond as soon as they are safe.
25.3 Financial and personal support. Employees directly affected by a declared crisis may receive an emergency salary advance without the usual waiting conditions, and may use the Employee Assistance Programme for themselves and their families. The Company may also arrange temporary accommodation for Employees whose homes are unsafe.
25.4 Client commitments. Each project maintains a continuity plan agreed with the client, covering alternate work locations, remote access and critical staffing. Employees named as critical in a continuity plan are informed in advance and may be asked to work from an alternate site.

text:
26. CAREGIVER SUPPORT
26.1 Flexible hours for parents. An Employee who is a parent of a child below three years of age may, with the Reporting Manager's agreement, work flexible hours outside the core hours, provided client commitments are met. The arrangement is recorded on the NPP and reviewed every six months.
26.2 Return-to-work support. An Employee returning from maternity or adoption leave may work a phased schedule for the first four weeks by agreement with the Reporting Manager, and is offered a return-to-work conversation with the HR Business Partner. Performance goals for the year are prorated for the period of leave.
26.3 Care for family members. An Employee caring for a seriously ill member of the Immediate Family may request temporary remote work or a temporary reduction in travel. The HR Business Partner will explore options such as Earned Leave, Leave Without Pay or a sabbatical under the Leave Policy where the need is extended.

text:
28. COMPANY ASSETS
28.1 Care of assets. Laptops, phones, access cards and other equipment issued to an Employee remain the property of the Company. They are to be used for Company work, kept secure, and never left unattended in vehicles or public places.
28.2 Loss or damage. Loss or damage is reported to the IT Service Desk immediately and, in the case of theft, to the police, with a copy of the police report uploaded on the NPP within 48 hours. Where loss results from negligence, the Company may recover the depreciated value of the asset, which for a laptop is reduced by 25 per cent of the purchase value for each completed year of use.
28.3 Return of assets. All assets are returned on the last day of service or when requested. The value of an asset not returned is recovered from the full and final settlement.

29. COMMUNICATION NORMS
29.1 E-mail and chat. Company e-mail and the approved chat tool are used for business communication. Client information is shared only through channels approved for that client. Employees do not use personal messaging applications to share Company or client information.
29.2 After-hours messages. Except for Employees on shift or on call, no Employee is expected to reply to non-urgent messages between 8:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. or on weekly offs. Managers are asked to schedule messages for the next Working Day and to use a phone call for genuine emergencies.
29.3 Meetings. Meetings are scheduled within core hours where possible, have an agenda, and end with agreed actions. Cameras are encouraged but not mandatory, except for client meetings where the client requests them.
The stages above apply to general grievances under Clause 13.2. Sexual harassment complaints go directly to the Internal Committee, and ethics concerns to the Ethics Office.

text:
ANNEXURE D: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS FOR NEW JOINERS
D.1 When will I receive my first salary? Salary for the month of joining is paid on the last Working Day of that month if joining formalities, including bank details, are completed on the NPP by the 20th. Otherwise it is paid with the salary of the following month.
D.2 Can I take leave during probation? Casual Leave and Sick Leave can be taken from joining. Earned Leave accrues from joining but can be availed only after three months of service, except in an emergency approved by the HR Business Partner, as provided in the Leave Policy.
D.3 When is my health insurance active? From the date of joining, provided the dependants' details are entered on the NPP within 30 days. Dependants added later are covered only from the next policy renewal on 1 July, except a newborn or a new spouse added within 30 days of the event.

D.10 I am being asked to work very late every day. What should I do? Discuss workload with the Reporting Manager first. If the pattern continues, raise it with the HR Business Partner or through the grievance process in Clause 13.2. Employees in Grades L1 to L3 may be entitled to overtime payment under the Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy.
D.11 Can my spouse also work at Nexora? Yes. Relatives may be employed, but an Employee may not be in the reporting line of a relative, or take part in decisions about the relative's hiring, pay, rating or promotion. The relationship must be declared on the NPP under the conflict of interest declaration.
D.12 Do I get paid for working on a Saturday? Weekend work requires prior approval. Employees in Grades L1 to L4 may receive compensatory off under the Leave Policy, and those in Grades L1 to L3 may be eligible for overtime under the Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy. Employees in Grades L5 and above are not eligible for either.

ANNEXURE G: ILLUSTRATIVE WORKPLACE SCENARIOS
The scenarios below show how the values and policies apply in everyday situations. They are illustrations only; the governing policies decide any actual case.
G.1 A vendor offers a festival hamper. A vendor whose contract Priya manages sends a large festival hamper to her home. Priya should check the value against the gift limit in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, declare it on the NPP, and return it if it exceeds the limit or if a contract decision involving the vendor is pending. Accepting it silently would create at least the appearance of a conflict of interest.
G.2 A colleague asks for your login. A teammate who has lost access asks Arjun for his password to finish an urgent client delivery. Arjun must refuse, even though the request is well meant, and help the colleague raise an urgent request with the IT Service Desk. Every action on a system is attributed to the account holder.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
1. POLICY STATEMENT
1.1 Commitment. The Company is committed to a Workplace free from Sexual Harassment, where every person is treated with dignity. Sexual Harassment is a violation of the fundamental rights to equality and to life with dignity, and is also misconduct under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004). The Company has zero tolerance for Sexual Harassment and for retaliation against anyone who raises a concern.
1.2 Legal framework. This Policy is framed in accordance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 and the rules made under it. Where this Policy is silent or inconsistent with the Act or the Rules, the Act and the Rules prevail.
1.3 What this Policy does. This Policy explains what Sexual Harassment is, how the Internal Committee is constituted, how a complaint is made and inquired into, the timelines at each stage, the relief available during an inquiry, the action that follows, and the protection given to Complainants and witnesses.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
2. SCOPE
2.1 Who is protected. This Policy protects every Aggrieved Woman, whether she is an Employee, a consultant, a trainee, an intern, a visitor, a candidate for interview, or an employee of a client, vendor or contractor, who is subjected to Sexual Harassment at a Workplace of the Company or by an Employee.
2.2 Protection limited to women. The complaint and inquiry procedure under this Policy is available to women, as provided in the Act. Complaints of harassment by or against persons of any gender that are not within the Act are dealt with under the grievance procedure described in the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002) and the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).
2.3 Who may be a Respondent. A complaint may be made against any Employee, irrespective of Grade, including a member of the senior leadership. Where the Respondent is not an Employee, for example an employee of a client or a vendor, the Internal Committee receives the complaint and the Company takes up the matter with the Respondent's employer, and supports the Complainant in any process of that employer or of the Local Committee.
2.4 Where the Policy applies. This Policy applies at every Workplace as defined in Clause 3.10, at all locations of the Company in India, whether the conduct occurs during or outside working hours.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
4. UNDERSTANDING SEXUAL HARASSMENT
4.1 The test is the impact. Whether conduct is Sexual Harassment is judged by whether it was unwelcome to the recipient, not by the intention of the person engaging in it. Conduct may be Sexual Harassment even if it happened once, even if the recipient did not object at the time, and even if others present did not find it offensive.
4.2 Examples. Examples of conduct that may amount to Sexual Harassment include: (a) touching, patting, pinching or brushing against a person, or standing unnecessarily close, where this is unwelcome; (b) comments or jokes about a person's body, appearance, clothing, sexual life or sexual orientation, or sexual innuendo; (c) repeated requests for dates or personal meetings after the person has shown disinterest; (d) sending or displaying sexually explicit messages, images, memes, videos or links, including in chat groups; (e) staring, leering, whistling or making sexual gestures; (f) suggesting that a rating, promotion, allocation or extension of contract depends on a personal or sexual relationship; and (g) following, repeatedly calling or messaging a person, or contacting a person on social media, in a manner that is unwelcome.
4.3 What is not Sexual Harassment. Legitimate feedback on performance, allocation of work, or a decision under a Company policy is not Sexual Harassment unless it is connected with conduct of a sexual nature. A consensual relationship between adults is not Sexual Harassment, but a relationship within a reporting line must be declared under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004), and conduct that was once welcome can become unwelcome.

text:
5. INTERNAL COMMITTEE
5.1 Constitution. The Company has constituted an Internal Committee at each of its locations, in writing, in accordance with Section 4 of the Act. Each Internal Committee consists of: (a) a Presiding Officer, who is a woman employed at a senior level at the location; (b) not less than two members from amongst Employees, preferably committed to the cause of women or having experience in social work or legal knowledge; and (c) one external member from a non-governmental organisation or association committed to the cause of women, or a person familiar with issues relating to Sexual Harassment.
5.2 Composition rules. At least one half of the members of each Internal Committee are women. Members hold office for a term not exceeding three years. The external member is paid a fee for each sitting, as permitted by the Rules. A member who is a party to, or has a conflict of interest in, a complaint withdraws from that complaint and is replaced for that complaint by a member nominated by the Presiding Officer.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
6. MAKING A COMPLAINT
6.1 Who may complain. An Aggrieved Woman may make a complaint of Sexual Harassment to the Internal Committee. She may first speak informally to any member of the Internal Committee, the HR Business Partner or the Employee Assistance Programme for guidance, and doing so does not amount to making a complaint.
6.2 Time limit. A complaint is made in writing within three months from the date of the incident and, in the case of a series of incidents, within three months from the date of the last incident. The Internal Committee may extend the time limit by a further period not exceeding three months if it is satisfied that circumstances prevented the Aggrieved Woman from complaining within the first period, recording its reasons in writing.

6.3 Form of complaint. A complaint is submitted in the form in Annexure A, or in any written form, by e-mail to the Internal Committee or in a sealed envelope addressed to the Presiding Officer. It should describe the incidents, dates, places and any witnesses, and attach any documents or messages available. Where the Aggrieved Woman cannot make the complaint in writing, the Presiding Officer or any member renders all reasonable assistance to her to reduce it to writing.
6.4 Complaint on behalf of the Aggrieved Woman. Where the Aggrieved Woman is unable to make a complaint on account of physical or mental incapacity, or death, or otherwise, her legal heir, a relative, a friend, a co-worker or another person specified in the Rules may make the complaint, with her written consent where the Rules require it.
6.5 Complaints received elsewhere. A manager, HR Business Partner or any other Employee who receives a complaint or disclosure of Sexual Harassment forwards it to the Internal Committee within one Working Day, shares it with no one else, and takes no action on it personally.

6.5 Complaints received elsewhere. A manager, HR Business Partner or any other Employee who receives a complaint or disclosure of Sexual Harassment forwards it to the Internal Committee within one Working Day, shares it with no one else, and takes no action on it personally.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
7. CONCILIATION
7.1 At the request of the Aggrieved Woman only. Before starting an inquiry, the Internal Committee may, at the request of the Aggrieved Woman and only at her request, take steps to settle the matter between her and the Respondent through conciliation. The Internal Committee does not suggest or encourage conciliation.
7.2 No monetary settlement. No monetary settlement may be made as a basis of conciliation.
7.3 Effect of settlement. Where a settlement is arrived at, the Internal Committee records it and forwards it to the Company for appropriate action, and provides copies to the Aggrieved Woman and the Respondent. No further inquiry is conducted, unless the Aggrieved Woman informs the Internal Committee that a term of the settlement has not been complied with, in which case the Internal Committee proceeds with the inquiry.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
8. INQUIRY
8.1 Notice to the Respondent. The Internal Committee sends a copy of the complaint to the Respondent within seven Days of receiving it. The Respondent files a reply with a list of documents and the names and addresses of witnesses within ten Days of receiving the copy.
8.2 Principles of natural justice. The inquiry is conducted in accordance with the principles of natural justice. Each party is given an opportunity to be heard, to present evidence and witnesses, and to receive a copy of the findings. The parties may not be represented by a legal practitioner at any stage of the proceedings before the Internal Committee.
8.3 Powers. For the purpose of the inquiry, the Internal Committee has the powers vested in a civil court in respect of summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person, examining a person on oath, and requiring the discovery and production of documents. Employees are required to cooperate with the inquiry.

text:
8.4 Absence of a party. Where the Complainant or the Respondent fails, without sufficient cause, to be present at three consecutive hearings convened by the Presiding Officer, the Internal Committee may terminate the proceedings or give an ex parte decision, after giving fifteen Days' written notice to the party concerned.
8.5 Time for completing the inquiry. The inquiry is completed within ninety Days of the receipt of the complaint. The Internal Committee provides its report of findings and recommendations to the Company and to both parties within ten Days of the completion of the inquiry. The Company acts on the recommendations within sixty Days of receiving the report. The complete sequence of steps is shown in Annexure B.
8.6 Complaints that may also be offences. Where the conduct complained of may also be an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 or any other law, the Internal Committee informs the Aggrieved Woman of her right to report it to the police, and the Company assists her if she decides to do so. The Company itself reports the matter to the police where it is required by law to do so.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
9. INTERIM RELIEF
9.1 Relief during the inquiry. During the pendency of an inquiry, on a written request by the Aggrieved Woman, the Internal Committee may recommend to the Company to: (a) transfer the Aggrieved Woman or the Respondent to another team, shift or location; (b) grant leave to the Aggrieved Woman of up to three months, in addition to the leave to which she is otherwise entitled under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001); and (c) restrain the Respondent from reporting on the work performance of the Aggrieved Woman, or from writing her performance review, and assign that responsibility to another officer.
9.2 Implementation. The Company implements a recommendation for interim relief within five Working Days and informs the Internal Committee. Interim relief is not a finding against the Respondent and does not affect the Respondent's pay.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
10. OUTCOME AND ACTION
10.1 Where the allegation is proved. Where the Internal Committee concludes that the allegation is proved, it recommends action under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004), which may include a written apology, a warning, a reprimand or censure, withholding of promotion, pay increase or variable pay, termination of employment, undergoing counselling, or community service.
10.2 Compensation. The Internal Committee may also recommend deduction from the salary of the Respondent of such sum as it considers appropriate to be paid to the Aggrieved Woman, having regard to the mental trauma, pain, suffering and emotional distress caused to her; the loss of career opportunity; medical expenses; and the income and financial status of the Respondent. The sum may be paid in a lump sum or in instalments.
10.3 Where the allegation is not proved. Where the Internal Committee concludes that the allegation is not proved, it recommends that no action is required. The Company ensures that neither party suffers any consequence merely because a complaint was made or defended.
10.4 False or malicious complaints. Where the Internal Committee concludes that a complaint was made with malicious intent, knowing it to be false, or on the basis of a forged or misleading document, it may recommend action against the person who made it. A mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof does not attract such action. Malicious intent must be established through an inquiry before any action is recommended.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
11. CONFIDENTIALITY
11.1 What is confidential. The identity and addresses of the Aggrieved Woman, the Respondent and the witnesses, the contents of the complaint, the conciliation and inquiry proceedings, the recommendations of the Internal Committee and the action taken by the Company are confidential and are not published, communicated or made known to the public, the press or the media in any manner. Information on the justice secured may be disseminated without disclosing names or identifying details.
11.2 Breach of confidentiality. Any person who breaches confidentiality under this Section is liable to action under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004), and the Company may recover a penalty from that person as provided in the Rules.
11.3 Records. Complaint files are kept by the Presiding Officer in a restricted repository to which only members of the Internal Committee have access, and are retained for eight years after closure.

text:
12. APPEAL
12.1 Right of appeal. Any person aggrieved by the recommendations of the Internal Committee, or by the non-implementation of the recommendations, may prefer an appeal to the appellate authority notified under the Act within ninety Days of the recommendations.
12.2 Pending appeal. The Company implements the recommendations unless an appellate authority stays them. An Employee who files an appeal informs the Presiding Officer so that the record can be preserved.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
13. PROTECTION AGAINST RETALIATION
13.1 No victimisation. No Complainant, witness, member of the Internal Committee or person who assists in an inquiry shall be victimised, discriminated against or subjected to any adverse action in work allocation, rating, promotion, transfer or continuation of employment for doing so.
13.2 Reporting retaliation. Any retaliation is reported to the Presiding Officer or the Ethics Office. Retaliation is treated as a separate act of misconduct and dealt with under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004), independently of the outcome of the original complaint.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
14. RESPONSIBILITIES AND AWARENESS
14.1 The Company. The Company provides a safe working environment; displays at each Workplace the consequences of Sexual Harassment and the composition of the Internal Committee; organises workshops and awareness programmes for Employees and orientation programmes for members of the Internal Committee; provides the Internal Committee with the facilities it needs; and assists in securing the attendance of the Respondent and witnesses.
14.2 Managers. Managers set the tone for respectful conduct, intervene when they observe inappropriate behaviour, forward any complaint to the Internal Committee as required by Clause 6.5, and ensure that no Employee is disadvantaged for raising a concern.
14.3 Every Employee. Every Employee is responsible for treating colleagues with respect, for speaking up or supporting a colleague who is being harassed, for cooperating with an inquiry, and for keeping inquiry matters confidential.
14.4 Training. Every Employee completes the POSH module on joining and every year thereafter. Members of the Internal Committee complete an advanced programme on inquiry procedure within 60 Days of appointment and a refresher every year.
14.5 Annual report. Each Internal Committee prepares an annual report giving the number of complaints received, disposed of and pending for more than ninety Days, and the awareness programmes held. The Company submits the report to the District Officer and includes the number of cases in its annual report, as required by the Act.

text:
15. SPECIAL SITUATIONS
15.1 Complaint against a senior leader. Where the Respondent is in Grade L8 or is a member of the leadership team, the Presiding Officer informs the Chief People Officer, or where the Chief People Officer is the Respondent, the Chair of the Audit Committee of the Board, so that the Respondent's authority cannot be used to influence the inquiry. The inquiry follows the same procedure and timelines as any other complaint.
15.2 Both parties in the same team. Where the Complainant and the Respondent work in the same team, the HR Business Partner, on the request of the Internal Committee, arranges for them not to attend the same meetings during the inquiry, without disadvantage to the Complainant and without this being treated as a finding against the Respondent.

text:
15.3 The Complainant or the Respondent leaves the Company. The resignation or separation of either party does not end an inquiry that has begun. The Internal Committee completes the inquiry, and its findings are recorded. Where the Respondent has left, the recommendations are recorded in the Respondent's employment file and considered if the Respondent seeks re-employment.
15.4 More than one complaint against the same Respondent. Where two or more complaints are received against the same Respondent, the Internal Committee may hear them together if the Complainants agree, while keeping the identity of each Complainant confidential from the others where requested. Each complaint is decided on its own evidence.
15.5 Complaints relating to online conduct. Screenshots, chat exports, call recordings and e-mail are accepted as evidence. The Internal Committee may ask the IT Service Desk to preserve relevant Company records, without accessing their content, as soon as a complaint is received.
15.6 Withdrawal of a complaint. A Complainant may ask to withdraw a complaint at any stage. The Internal Committee meets the Complainant privately to confirm that the request is voluntary and not the result of pressure. Where it has reason to believe that pressure has been applied, it records its concern and may recommend action for retaliation under Section 13.

title: Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH)
text:
ANNEXURE C: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS AND ILLUSTRATIONS
C.1 Does this Policy cover messages sent late at night on a personal phone? Yes, if the messages arise out of the working relationship. A Workplace under Clause 3.10 includes messaging applications and groups used by colleagues, on any device and at any hour. For example, unwelcome sexual messages from a colleague on a personal messaging application at 11 p.m. on a Sunday are within this Policy.
C.2 The incident happened at a team dinner that the team paid for. Is it covered? Yes. An off-site or team event is a Workplace whether or not it is organised or paid for by the Company, provided it is connected with work.
C.3 Can I complain about something that happened five months ago? The time limit is three months from the incident, or from the last incident in a series. The Internal Committee may extend it by up to a further three months if circumstances prevented a complaint earlier, so a complaint five months after the incident may be accepted with reasons. You should approach the Internal Committee as soon as you can.
C.4 Will my manager be told about my complaint? Only to the extent strictly necessary, for example to implement interim relief. The complaint and the inquiry are confidential under Section 11.
C.5 I only want the behaviour to stop. Do I have to file a formal complaint? No. You may speak to a member of the Internal Committee for guidance, and you may ask for conciliation under Section 7. The Internal Committee does not start an inquiry without a complaint, but it may arrange awareness sessions for a team without naming anyone.
C.6 Can my lawyer attend the hearing? No. Legal practitioners may not represent either party before the Internal Committee under Clause 8.2. You may consult a lawyer outside the proceedings.

For example, unwelcome sexual messages from a colleague on a personal messaging application at 11 p.m. on a Sunday are within this Policy.
C.2 The incident happened at a team dinner that the team paid for. Is it covered? Yes. An off-site or team event is a Workplace whether or not it is organised or paid for by the Company, provided it is connected with work.
C.3 Can I complain about something that happened five months ago? The time limit is three months from the incident, or from the last incident in a series. The Internal Committee may extend it by up to a further three months if circumstances prevented a complaint earlier, so a complaint five months after the incident may be accepted with reasons. You should approach the Internal Committee as soon as you can.
C.4 Will my manager be told about my complaint? Only to the extent strictly necessary, for example to implement interim relief. The complaint and the inquiry are confidential under Section 11.
C.5 I only want the behaviour to stop. Do I have to file a formal complaint? No. You may speak to a member of the Internal Committee for guidance, and you may ask for conciliation under Section 7. The Internal Committee does not start an inquiry without a complaint, but it may arrange awareness sessions for a team without naming anyone.
C.6 Can my lawyer attend the hearing? No. Legal practitioners may not represent either party before the Internal Committee under Clause 8.2. You may consult a lawyer outside the proceedings.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
1. INTRODUCTION
1.1 Purpose. This Code sets out the standards of conduct that the Company expects of every Employee. It explains how to recognise and handle conflicts of interest, gifts, confidential information and other ethical questions, how to raise concerns, and what happens when the Code is breached. The Code cannot anticipate every situation; where it is silent, Employees are expected to act in a way they would be comfortable seeing reported publicly.
1.2 Application. This Code applies to every Employee at every location, including when working from home, at a client site or while travelling, and in personal conduct that affects the Company's reputation or business relationships. Consultants, contractors and vendors are bound by the Supplier Code of Conduct, which reflects the principles of this Code.
1.3 Relationship with law and other policies. Where applicable law imposes a stricter requirement than this Code, the law applies. The Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) (NTL/HR/POL/003) governs complaints of sexual harassment, and the IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy (NTL/HR/POL/009) governs information security; this Code summarises their requirements for convenience.
1.4 Responsibility for the Code. The Chief Ethics Officer is responsible for the interpretation of this Code, maintains the conflict of interest and gift registers, and reports to the Audit Committee of the Board every quarter on concerns raised and their outcome.

2.1 "Business Associate" means any client, prospective client, vendor, supplier, subcontractor, consultant, agent or partner of the Company, and any of their employees or representatives.
2.2 "Conflict of Interest" means a situation in which an Employee's personal interest, or the interest of a Relative, interferes or could reasonably appear to interfere with the Employee's duty to act in the best interest of the Company.
2.3 "Designated Person" means an Employee who, by reason of role, is likely to have access to Unpublished Price Sensitive Information, namely: every Employee in Grade L8; every Employee in Grades L6 and L7 in the Finance, Legal, Company Secretarial, Investor Relations and Strategy functions; the executive assistants of Employees in Grade L8; and any other Employee notified in writing by the Company Secretary. 3. OUR STANDARDS
3.1 Integrity. Employees are honest in all dealings, do not misrepresent facts to clients, colleagues or authorities, and correct errors promptly when they discover them. Pressure to meet a deadline or a target never justifies a breach of this Code.
3.2 Compliance with law. Employees comply with the laws of India and of any other country in which they work, including laws on employment, tax, data protection, anti-corruption, competition, export control and securities. Where an Employee is unsure whether an action is lawful, the Employee consults the Legal department before acting.
3.3 Managers' additional responsibilities. Managers lead by example, ensure that their teams understand this Code, create an environment in which concerns can be raised without fear, and escalate to the Ethics Office any concern reported to them that may involve a breach of this Code. A manager who ignores a reported breach is personally accountable.
3.4 Asking for guidance. An Employee facing an ethical question may ask the Reporting Manager, the HR Business Partner, the Legal department or the Ethics Office at ethics@nexora.example. Guidance is given in writing on request, and an Employee who acts in good faith on written guidance from the Ethics Office is not in breach of this Code.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
4. CONFLICTS OF INTEREST
4.1 General rule. Employees avoid situations that create a Conflict of Interest. Where a Conflict of Interest cannot be avoided, it is disclosed before the Employee takes any decision or action connected with it, and the Employee withdraws from that decision unless the Ethics Office directs otherwise.
4.2 Declarations. Every Employee makes a conflict of interest declaration on the NPP on joining and each year by 31 May, and makes an additional declaration within 15 days of any change in circumstances. A declaration of "no conflict" is also required. Failure to declare is itself a breach of this Code, even where no harm results.
4.3 Relatives at work. A Relative of an Employee may be employed by the Company, but an Employee shall not be in the reporting line of a Relative, and shall not take part in any decision about a Relative's hiring, allocation, rating, promotion, pay or discipline. The same applies to a person with whom the Employee is in a close personal relationship.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
4.4 Personal relationships. A romantic or close personal relationship between Employees where one reports directly or indirectly to the other, or can influence the other's work or pay, is declared by the senior party to the HR Business Partner within 15 days. The Company then changes the reporting line or responsibilities, without adverse effect on the junior party.
4.5 Financial interests. An Employee declares any financial interest, held directly or through a Relative, in a Business Associate or a competitor where the interest exceeds one per cent of the equity of that entity or Rs. 10,00,000 in value, whichever is lower. Investments in listed mutual funds are not required to be declared.
4.6 Business Associates connected with an Employee. An Employee shall not select, approve or manage a vendor or subcontractor in which the Employee or a Relative has an interest or is employed. The Procurement function records any such connection and assigns the decision to another approver.
4.7 Outside directorships. An Employee shall not accept a directorship, partnership or advisory role in any entity other than a non-profit organisation or a private company of the Employee's own family without the prior approval of the Chief Ethics Officer. Directorship of a Business Associate or a competitor is not approved.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
5. OUTSIDE EMPLOYMENT AND ACTIVITIES
5.1 No outside employment. An Employee devotes full working time to the Company and shall not take up any other employment, paid assignment, consultancy, freelance work or business, whether during or outside working hours and whether or not the work competes with the Company, without the prior written approval of the Chief Ethics Officer. Such approval is ordinarily not given.
5.2 Activities that do not need approval. The following do not require approval, provided they do not use Company time, assets or confidential information, and do not involve a Business Associate: unpaid community or religious service; management of the Employee's own personal investments; and unpaid membership of professional bodies and alumni associations.

An Employee may write articles, speak at conferences and contribute to open-source projects in a personal capacity, with the Reporting Manager's approval where the subject relates to the Employee's work. 6.1 Principle. An Employee shall not offer, give, solicit or accept any Gift that could influence, or reasonably appear to influence, a business decision. Gifts shall never be solicited in any amount.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
7. ANTI-BRIBERY AND ANTI-CORRUPTION
7.1 Zero tolerance. The Company prohibits bribery in any form. No Employee shall offer, promise, give, request or accept any undue advantage to or from any person, including a Government Official, to obtain or retain business or any improper advantage. Bribery is a criminal offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, which also makes a commercial organisation liable where a person associated with it gives a bribe for its benefit.
7.2 Facilitation payments. Small unofficial payments to speed up routine government actions, such as issuing a permit or clearing goods, are bribes and are prohibited, even where they are customary. An Employee asked for such a payment refuses and reports the request to the Ethics Office. The only exception is a payment made under immediate threat to personal safety, which is reported within 24 hours.

8. INSIDER TRADING
8.1 Legal framework. The equity shares of the Company are listed on recognised stock exchanges in India. Trading in securities while in possession of UPSI, and the communication of UPSI except for legitimate purposes, are prohibited by the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The Company's detailed Code of Conduct for Prevention of Insider Trading, maintained by the Company Secretary, prevails over this Section in case of inconsistency.
8.2 Rules for every Employee. Every Employee, whether or not a Designated Person, shall not trade in the securities of the Company, or of a client or other listed company, while in possession of UPSI about it, and shall not pass UPSI to anyone, including a Relative or friend, or recommend that anyone trade on the basis of it.

8.3 Designated Persons. 9. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
9.1 Confidential information. Information about the Company, its clients, its Business Associates and its Employees that is not public is confidential. Employees use it only for the purpose for which it was provided, share it only with those who need it for their work, and protect it in accordance with the IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy (NTL/HR/POL/009). The obligation continues after employment ends.
9.2 Client information. Client information is used only for the client's project and is never shared with another client, used for a proposal to another client, or taken outside approved systems. Where a client contract imposes stricter obligations, the contract prevails.
9.3 Intellectual property. All work product created by an Employee in the course of employment, or using Company resources, including software, designs, documents and inventions, belongs to the Company or, where the contract so provides, to the client. Employees disclose inventions to the Legal department and assist in securing rights in them.
9.4 Third-party material. Employees respect the intellectual property of others. Software, images, text and data are used only under a valid licence, and confidential information belonging to a previous employer shall not be brought to or used at the Company.

10. FAIR DEALING
10.1 Clients. Employees represent the Company's services honestly, do not promise what the Company cannot deliver, and report any delivery risk to the client through the agreed governance process.
10.2 Competitors. Employees do not agree or discuss with competitors any matter relating to prices, bids, allocation of clients or markets, or salaries of Employees, as such conduct may breach the Competition Act, 2002. Competitive information is obtained only from public or legitimate sources.
10.3 Vendors. Vendors are selected on merit through the procurement process. Employees do not disclose one vendor's bid to another and treat vendors courteously and fairly.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics

12. RESPECTFUL WORKPLACE
12.1 Dignity at work. Every Employee treats others with dignity and courtesy. Discrimination on the basis of gender, religion, caste, region, language, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status or any other characteristic protected by law is prohibited.
12.2 Harassment and bullying. Harassment, bullying, intimidation, abusive language, threats and humiliation, whether in person, in writing or online, are prohibited. Repeated public criticism intended to humiliate, deliberate exclusion from work, and spreading malicious rumours are examples of bullying.
12.3 Violence and substances. Violence or threats of violence, possession of weapons on Company premises, and working under the influence of alcohol or drugs are prohibited. Alcohol may be served at Company events only with the approval of the Business Unit Head and within the limits set by the organisers.
12.4 Time limit for grievances. Any grievance of harassment, including sexual harassment, discrimination or bullying, shall be reported to the HR Business Partner or the appropriate committee within 30 days of the incident, so that it can be investigated while evidence is available. Grievances reported after 30 days may be considered at the discretion of the Chief Ethics Officer.

13. SPEAKING UP AND WHISTLEBLOWER PROTECTION
13.1 Duty to report. An Employee who becomes aware of a breach or suspected breach of this Code, of any law, or of any Company policy reports it through one of the channels in Clause 13.2. Reporting in good faith is always protected, even if the concern turns out to be unfounded.
13.2 Channels. Concerns may be raised with the Reporting Manager, the HR Business Partner, the Ethics Office at ethics@nexora.example, or the ethics hotline at 1800-000-0000 (extension 7), which is operated by an independent provider and accepts anonymous reports. 13.3 Handling of concerns. The Ethics Office acknowledges a concern within three Working Days, completes a preliminary review within 15 Working Days, and where an investigation is warranted, completes it ordinarily within 60 days. The Whistleblower is informed of the outcome in general terms, subject to the privacy of others.
