15. DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURE
15.1 Breach of the Code. A breach of this Code, of any Company policy or of the law in connection with employment is misconduct. Examples of minor and major misconduct, and the range of penalties, are given in Table 3. The penalty in each case depends on the seriousness of the conduct, its impact, the Employee's intent and previous record, and any mitigating circumstances.
15.2 Procedure. Except for counselling, no penalty is imposed without following a fair procedure: (a) the Employee is issued a show-cause notice setting out the allegations and the material relied upon; (b) the Employee submits a written reply within seven days, which may be extended once on request; (c) where the allegation is disputed and a major penalty is contemplated, an inquiry officer, who is not in the Employee's reporting line, conducts an inquiry at which the Employee may present evidence and be accompanied by a colleague; and (d) the disciplinary authority decides on the basis of the inquiry report and informs the Employee in writing of the decision and the reasons.

15.1 Breach of the Code. A breach of this Code, of any Company policy or of the law in connection with employment is misconduct. Examples of minor and major misconduct, and the range of penalties, are given in Table 3. The penalty in each case depends on the seriousness of the conduct, its impact, the Employee's intent and previous record, and any mitigating circumstances.
15.2 Procedure. Except for counselling, no penalty is imposed without following a fair procedure: (a) the Employee is issued a show-cause notice setting out the allegations and the material relied upon; (b) the Employee submits a written reply within seven days, which may be extended once on request; (c) where the allegation is disputed and a major penalty is contemplated, an inquiry officer, who is not in the Employee's reporting line, conducts an inquiry at which the Employee may present evidence and be accompanied by a colleague; and (d) the disciplinary authority decides on the basis of the inquiry report and informs the Employee in writing of the decision and the reasons.

section_title: Money Laundering, Sanctions and Export Control
text:
17. MONEY LAUNDERING, SANCTIONS AND EXPORT CONTROL
17.1 Anti-money laundering. The Company does not facilitate money laundering or the financing of terrorism. Employees are alert to unusual payment requests from Business Associates, such as payment to a third party, payment in cash, payment to an account in a different country from the Business Associate, or overpayment followed by a request for refund, and report them to Finance before processing.
17.2 Screening of Business Associates. New clients, vendors and partners are screened by the Legal department against sanctions and watch lists before a contract is signed, and existing Business Associates are re-screened each year. No Employee may start work for, or place an order with, a Business Associate that has not cleared screening.
17.3 Sanctions. The Company complies with sanctions imposed by India and by the United Nations, and with the sanctions of other countries that apply to its clients' contracts. Employees do not provide services to, travel for work to, or transfer technology to, a sanctioned country, entity or person without the prior written approval of the Legal department.
17.4 Export control. Certain software, encryption technology and technical data are subject to export control laws of India and of the country of origin. Employees working on client projects that involve controlled technology follow the access restrictions notified for the project and do not share controlled technical data with colleagues who have not been cleared for it, including colleagues of another nationality where the client contract so requires.

text:
18. HUMAN RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBLE SUPPLY CHAIN
18.1 Respect for human rights. The Company respects internationally recognised human rights, and does not tolerate forced labour, bonded labour, human trafficking or child labour in its operations or in its supply chain. The Company does not employ any person below the age of eighteen years in any role.
18.2 Contract workers. Employees who manage housekeeping, security, catering or other contracted services ensure that the contractor pays its workers at least the minimum wages applicable in the State, provides the statutory benefits, and complies with the contract labour legislation in force. Evidence of payment is checked by Facilities every quarter before the contractor's invoice is approved.
18.3 Supplier Code of Conduct. Every vendor accepts the Supplier Code of Conduct, which covers labour practices, health and safety, environment, anti-bribery and data protection. An Employee who learns that a vendor is not complying informs Procurement, which may audit the vendor and suspend orders.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
19. HEALTH, SAFETY AND ENVIRONMENT
19.1 Safe conduct. Employees follow the safety rules at every Workplace, take part in fire drills, keep exits and corridors clear, and report hazards, accidents and near misses promptly through the Facilities module of the NPP. No Employee may disable a safety device or override a safety procedure.
19.2 Environment. Employees support the Company's commitment to reduce energy use, water use and waste, by switching off equipment when not in use, using the waste segregation bins, and returning old electronic equipment only through the IT Service Desk for certified recycling. Printing is kept to what is necessary.
19.3 Travel safety. Employees travelling for work follow the Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy (NTL/HR/POL/007), register their itinerary on the NPP, and do not drive themselves on work journeys of more than 250 kilometres without the approval of the Reporting Manager.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
20. CONDUCT AWAY FROM THE OFFICE
20.1 At client sites. At a client site, Employees represent the Company. They follow the client's security and conduct rules where the Company has accepted them, use only the systems and access granted for the project, and do not discuss one client's affairs at another client's premises.
20.2 At Company events. The standards of this Code apply at team outings, off-sites, celebrations and conferences, including those held after working hours or at external venues. Organisers ensure that events are inclusive, that alcohol, where approved, is served responsibly, and that transport home is available after late events.
20.3 While travelling. On business travel Employees behave courteously towards hosts, co-travellers and service staff, respect local laws and customs, and are mindful that their conduct reflects on the Company even outside working hours.
20.4 Conduct outside work. The Company does not seek to regulate Employees' private lives. However, conduct outside work that results in a criminal conviction, involves harassment of a colleague, or brings the Company into public disrepute may be treated as misconduct. An Employee who is arrested or charged with a criminal offence informs the HR Business Partner within 48 hours, and the information is kept confidential.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
21. REMOTE WORK AND VIRTUAL MEETINGS
21.1 Same standards online. The standards of this Code apply equally to conduct on video calls, chat tools and e-mail. Comments, images and reactions posted in team channels are subject to the same rules on respect and harassment as conduct in the office.
21.2 Recording meetings. A meeting is recorded only after all participants have been informed at the start and, for client meetings, only with the client's consent. Recordings are stored only in approved repositories and deleted in accordance with the IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy (NTL/HR/POL/009). Automated transcription or note-taking tools are used only where approved by Information Security.
21.3 Working from home. Employees working from home ensure that family members and visitors cannot see or hear confidential client information, take calls from a private space, and do not allow others to use the Company laptop.

title: Code of Conduct and Ethics
text:
22. PERSONAL DATA
22.1 Handling personal data. Employees who handle personal data of colleagues, candidates, clients' customers or any other person access it only when required for their role, use it only for the purpose for which it was collected, and never download, copy, share or discuss it beyond that purpose. The rules are set out in the IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy (NTL/HR/POL/009).
22.2 Curiosity is not a purpose. Looking up the salary, rating, medical documents, address or personal details of a colleague on the NPP, a client system or any other system without a work reason is a breach of this Code, even if the system technically allows the access and even if the information is not shared further.
22.3 Breaches. Any suspected unauthorised access to or disclosure of personal data is reported to the IT Service Desk immediately, so that the Company can meet its legal obligations to notify, as described in the IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy (NTL/HR/POL/009).

ANNEXURE C: ETHICAL SCENARIOS AND GUIDANCE
The scenarios below illustrate how the Code applies. Where a scenario states an exception, the exception forms part of the Code.
C.1 A vendor offers a gift card during Diwali. A vendor sends an Employee in Procurement a gift card of Rs. 3,000 while the vendor's contract renewal is under negotiation. Although the value is within the limit, the Employee is involved in a negotiation with the vendor, so accepting it could appear to influence the decision. The Employee declines and records the offer.
C.2 Gifts at the Employee's own wedding. Personal gifts given to an Employee on the occasion of the Employee's own wedding or the birth of a child by colleagues or by personal friends are outside the Gift limits in Section 6. Gifts on such occasions from a Business Associate remain subject to the limits and must be recorded where required.

ANNEXURE D: ETHICAL DECISION CHECKLIST
Before acting in a situation that feels uncertain, ask the questions below. If the answer to any question is no, or if you are unsure, stop and seek guidance under Clause 3.4.
Table 4: Questions to ask before acting
Question: Is it legal, in every country involved? | Why it matters: Legality is the minimum standard, and laws differ between countries
Question: Is it consistent with this Code and the Company's policies? | Why it matters: The policies record what the Company has decided in advance
Question: Would I be comfortable if it were reported in the news or to my family? | Why it matters: A test of how others would see the action
Question: Would I be comfortable if my Reporting Manager, the client and the Ethics Office knew all the facts? | Why it matters: Actions that need to be hidden are rarely right
Question: Does it benefit me or a Relative at the expense of the Company, a client or a colleague? | Why it matters: A sign of a possible Conflict of Interest
Question: Would it still be acceptable if everyone in the Company did it? | Why it matters: A test of whether the action can be a standard
Question: Have I recorded what I did and why? | Why it matters: A written record protects the Employee who acts in good faith

title: Compensation and Benefits Policy
text:
1. PURPOSE AND PRINCIPLES
1.1 Purpose. This Policy sets out how Employees are paid, the components of pay, the statutory and Company benefits, the variable pay plan, the group insurance programme, the employee stock option scheme, and the annual pay review. It is read with each Employee's compensation letter, which states the individual amounts.
1.2 Principles. The Company pays competitively against the Indian IT services market for each Grade and skill, links a part of pay to Company and individual performance, and pays men and women equally for the same work or work of a similar nature, as required by the Code on Wages, 2019. Pay decisions are free from discrimination on any ground listed in the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).
1.3 Precedence. Where the compensation letter of an Employee differs from this Policy, the letter prevails for that Employee, unless the letter provides less than applicable law. Where this Policy differs from the summary of pay and benefits in the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002), this Policy prevails.
1.4 Confidentiality. Individual pay is confidential between the Employee and the Company. Employees may discuss their own pay if they wish, but Employees with access to pay data through their role shall not disclose any other Employee's pay.

2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Annual Fixed Pay" means the total of Basic Salary, house rent allowance, leave travel allowance, communication allowance and special allowance payable in a year, before deductions.
2.2 "Basic Salary" means the component of pay designated as basic in the compensation letter, which is 50 per cent of Annual Fixed Pay for every Grade.
2.3 "Cost to Company" (CTC) means Annual Fixed Pay, plus the employer's contributions to provident fund and, where applicable, the National Pension System, plus the provision for gratuity at 4.81 per cent of Basic Salary, plus Target Variable Pay. Group insurance premiums are borne by the Company in addition to CTC.
2.4 "Company Factor" means the multiplier between 0 and 1.3 approved by the Board for a Performance Year on the basis of the Company's revenue and operating margin against plan.

text:
3. SALARY STRUCTURE
3.1 Components. Annual Fixed Pay is divided into the components below. The percentages and amounts by Grade are set out in Table 1. (a) Basic Salary: 50 per cent of Annual Fixed Pay, so that wages as defined in the Code on Wages, 2019 are not less than half of total remuneration; (b) house rent allowance (HRA): 50 per cent of Basic Salary, paid at every location irrespective of whether the location is a Metro City; (c) leave travel allowance (LTA): a fixed annual amount by Grade, paid in equal monthly instalments; (d) communication allowance: a fixed monthly amount for Grades L5 to L8; and (e) special allowance: the balance of Annual Fixed Pay after the above components.

An illustrative breakup of CTC is given in Annexure A. Employer NPS is optional and is funded by restructuring the special allowance; it does not increase CTC.
3.2 House rent allowance and tax. HRA is paid at the same rate at every location. The income tax exemption on HRA, available only under the old tax regime, is the least of the HRA received, the rent paid minus 10 per cent of Basic Salary, and 50 per cent of Basic Salary for an Employee living in a Metro City or 40 per cent elsewhere. Payroll computes the exemption on the basis of the city in which the Employee pays rent, applying the definition of Metro City in Clause 2.6.
3.3 Meal card. An Employee may choose to receive up to Rs. 2,200 a month of the special allowance as a prepaid meal card, which may be used only for food and non-alcoholic beverages. The tax treatment of meal cards depends on the tax regime chosen and the limits under the Income-tax Rules.
3.4 Changes to the structure. An Employee may change the meal card and employer NPS elections once a year in April through the NPP. The structure is otherwise fixed and cannot be varied by individual request.

title: Compensation and Benefits Policy
text:
4. PAYROLL
4.1 Pay date and cut-off. Salary is credited on the last Working Day of each month. Inputs such as joining, leave without pay, arrears and claims approved by the 20th of a month are processed in that month's payroll; inputs received later are processed in the following month.
4.2 Payslip. The payslip, showing each component, deduction and year-to-date total, is available on the NPP on the pay date. An Employee who believes the payslip is incorrect raises a ticket in the Payroll category within 30 days; corrections are made in the next payroll.
4.3 Statutory deductions. The Company deducts income tax at source, the Employee's provident fund contribution, the Employee's ESI contribution where applicable, and professional tax where levied by the State, and remits them to the authorities within the time allowed by law.

text:
4.4 Professional tax by State. Professional tax is a State levy, and the amount deducted depends on the Employee's Base Location, as set out in Table 2. No professional tax is deducted for Employees based in Noida, because Uttar Pradesh does not levy professional tax on salaried employees.
Professional tax cannot exceed Rs. 2,500 in a year for any person, under the Constitution of India. State rates and thresholds change from time to time; payroll applies the rates in force.
4.5 Loss of pay. For each day of Leave Without Pay or unauthorised absence, fixed pay is reduced by one-thirtieth of the monthly fixed pay, irrespective of the number of days in the month.
4.6 Recoveries. Salary advances, notice period shortfall, unreturned assets and other amounts due to the Company are recovered from salary or the full and final settlement only as permitted by law and after informing the Employee of the amount and the reason.

4.5 Loss of pay. For each day of Leave Without Pay or unauthorised absence, fixed pay is reduced by one-thirtieth of the monthly fixed pay, irrespective of the number of days in the month.
4.6 Recoveries. Salary advances, notice period shortfall, unreturned assets and other amounts due to the Company are recovered from salary or the full and final settlement only as permitted by law and after informing the Employee of the amount and the reason.

title: Compensation and Benefits Policy
text:
7. GRATUITY
7.1 Eligibility. Gratuity is payable under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 to an Employee who leaves the Company by resignation, retirement or termination after not less than five years of continuous service. The five-year condition does not apply where employment ends by death or disablement due to accident or disease.
7.2 Amount. Gratuity is fifteen days of the last drawn Basic Salary for every completed year of service, calculated as Basic Salary multiplied by 15 and divided by 26, multiplied by the number of completed years. A part of a year exceeding six months is counted as a full year. Gratuity is subject to the ceiling of Rs. 20,00,000 in the Act.

7.3 Time of payment. Gratuity becomes payable on the date employment ends, and the Company pays it within 30 days of the date it becomes payable, whether or not the rest of the full and final settlement has been completed. If payment is delayed beyond this period, the Company pays simple interest at the rate notified under the Act.

8. VARIABLE PAY
8.1 Eligibility. Employees in Grades L2 to L8 are eligible for variable pay at the Target Variable Pay for their Grade in Table 1. Employees in Grade L1 are not eligible; Graduate Engineer Trainees receive a one-time completion bonus described in their offer letter instead.
8.2 Calculation. Variable pay for a Performance Year equals Target Variable Pay multiplied by the Company Factor and the Individual Factor. The Individual Factor for each rating is set out in Table 3.
8.3 Proration. An Employee who joins during a Performance Year receives variable pay prorated for the number of complete months of service in that year. Periods of maternity, adoption and paternity leave count as service for proration; periods of Leave Without Pay of more than 30 days do not.

An Employee in Grades L5 to L8 may elect an employer contribution to the Employee's National Pension System account of up to 10 per cent of Basic Salary, funded by an equivalent reduction in special allowance. The election is made on the NPP in April and applies for the Performance Year.
11.2 Tax. The employer contribution is eligible for deduction under section 80CCD(2) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, within the percentage of salary allowed for the tax regime chosen. Contributions above the limit are taxable.

title: Compensation and Benefits Policy
text:
12. ALLOWANCES AND OTHER BENEFITS
12.1 Leave travel allowance. LTA is paid monthly as part of Annual Fixed Pay. Under the old tax regime, an Employee may claim exemption for the cost of travel within India for the Employee and family, for two journeys in a block of four calendar years, by submitting tickets on the NPP by 15 January.
12.2 Leave condition for LTA. An LTA exemption claim is accepted only where the journey was undertaken during a spell of Earned Leave of at least 5 Working Days recorded on the NPP.
12.3 Communication allowance. Employees in Grades L5 to L8 receive a communication allowance towards mobile and internet costs, as shown in Table 1, and do not claim these costs separately. Employees in lower Grades on hybrid work claim internet reimbursement as described in the Employee Handbook
(NTL/HR/POL/002).
12.4 Car lease. An Employee in Grade L7 or L8 may lease a car through the Company's leasing partner by restructuring special allowance. The tax on the perquisite is calculated under the Income-tax Rules and deducted through payroll. The car and all costs remain within the Employee's CTC.

title: Compensation and Benefits Policy
text:
13. ANNUAL PAY REVIEW
13.1 Cycle. Pay is reviewed once a year. Revised pay is effective from 1 July and communicated through a revised compensation letter on the NPP by 30 June. Arrears, if any, are paid in the July payroll.
13.2 Increase guidelines. The budget for increases is approved by the Board each year. Within the budget, increases are guided by performance rating and by the Employee's position in the pay range for the Grade, as set out in Table 6.
The ranges are indicative and apply at a budget of 8 per cent. They are scaled up or down in proportion to the budget approved for the year.
13.3 Promotion increase. An Employee promoted on 1 July receives a promotion increase of 10 to 15 per cent of Annual Fixed Pay in addition to the merit increase, subject to the minimum of the pay range of the new Grade.
13.4 Pay equity review. Each year, before increases are finalised, Total Rewards reviews pay within each Grade and role for unexplained differences between men and women and between locations, and reports the result to the Chief People Officer with corrective proposals.

14. PAY RANGES AND OFFERS
14.1 Pay ranges. Each Grade has a pay range for Annual Fixed Pay, reviewed every year against market surveys for the Indian IT services industry. The ranges in force from 1 January 2025 are set out in Table 7. Ranges for niche skills may be extended by up to 20 per cent above the maximum with the approval of the Head, Total Rewards.
The ranges are the same at every location; the Company does not apply location differentials within India.
14.2 Offers to new Employees. An offer is made within the range for the Grade, taking into account the candidate's current pay, skills and the pay of Employees in the same role. An offer above the midpoint requires the approval of the Business Unit Head, and an offer above the maximum requires the approval of the Head, Total Rewards.
14.3 Joining bonus. A joining bonus may be offered to compensate a candidate for a bonus or benefit forfeited on leaving a previous employer. It is paid with the first salary and is recovered in full if the Employee resigns, or is terminated for misconduct, within 12 months of joining.
14.4 Retention bonus. A retention bonus may be awarded to an Employee in a critical role, in writing, specifying the amount, the retention period and the payment date. It is paid only if the Employee is on the rolls and not serving notice on the payment date, and is not pro-rated on early exit.

text:
15. STATUTORY BONUS
15.1 Eligibility. An Employee whose salary or wage, as defined in the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, does not exceed Rs. 21,000 a month and who has worked for at least 30 working days in the accounting year is entitled to statutory bonus for that year.
15.2 Amount and payment. Statutory bonus is paid at not less than 8.33 per cent and not more than 20 per cent of the salary or wage earned, calculated on a salary or wage of Rs. 7,000 a month or the minimum wage for the scheduled employment, whichever is higher. It is paid by 30 November following the end of the accounting year on 31 March.
15.3 Relationship with variable pay. Most Employees earn above the eligibility limit and are not entitled to statutory bonus. For an eligible Employee, statutory bonus is paid in addition to any variable pay, and variable pay is not reduced on account of it.

16. INCOME TAX ADMINISTRATION
16.1 Choice of tax regime. Each Employee chooses the old or the new tax regime for the purpose of monthly tax deduction, through the NPP in April or within 30 days of joining. If no choice is made, tax is deducted under the new regime, which is the default under the Income-tax Act.
16.2 Declarations and proofs. Under the old regime, the Employee declares proposed investments, rent and interest on housing loans on the NPP in April, and submits proofs, including rent receipts and the landlord's permanent account number where annual rent exceeds Rs. 1,00,000, by 15 January. Tax for the months of February and March is adjusted to reflect the proofs actually submitted.

17. PAY IN SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES
17.1 During paid leave. Full fixed pay is paid during all paid leave under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001). Leave Without Pay reduces pay as described in Clause 4.5.
17.2 During the notice period. An Employee serving notice continues to receive full pay and benefits until the last day of service. Where the Company waives the notice period, pay is made up to the last day of service as agreed; where the Employee does not serve the notice required, the shortfall is recovered as provided in the Separation and Exit Policy (NTL/HR/POL/008).
17.3 During suspension. An Employee suspended pending inquiry receives the subsistence allowance provided in the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004). Benefits under group insurance continue during suspension.

17.4 During a sabbatical. No salary is paid during a sabbatical. Group medical insurance for the Employee alone continues at the Company's cost, as provided in the Leave Policy, and provident fund contributions are suspended.

18. PAY ON ASSIGNMENTS ABROAD
18.1 Home-based pay. An Employee on an assignment abroad of more than 90 days under the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002) continues to receive Annual Fixed Pay in India, and provident fund contributions continue. The Employee also receives a host allowance, housing and other benefits stated in the assignment letter, paid in the host currency.
18.2 Host allowance. The host allowance is set by country group, as shown in Table 8, to meet reasonable daily living costs other than housing. It is not part of Annual Fixed Pay, is not counted for gratuity, variable pay or pay review, and stops on the last day of the assignment.
Housing is provided separately through a Company-leased apartment. Countries not listed are assigned to a group by the Head, Total Rewards.
18.3 Tax equalisation. Assignments of more than 183 days in a year are tax-equalised: the Employee bears the tax the Employee would have paid in India on home-based pay, and the Company bears any additional tax in the host country. Tax returns in both countries are prepared by the Company's appointed advisor.

19. LOANS AND ADVANCES
19.1 Salary advance. The interest-free salary advance for medical emergencies described in the Employee Handbook is administered by Payroll and recovered in not more than six equal monthly instalments.
19.2 Emergency loan. A Confirmed Employee in Grades L1 to L4 facing hospitalisation of the Employee or a member of the Immediate Family, or damage to the Employee's home from a natural calamity, may apply for an interest-free emergency loan of up to Rs. 2,00,000, recovered in not more than 24 monthly instalments. Only one emergency loan may be outstanding at a time.
19.3 Tax on loans. An interest-free loan is a taxable perquisite, except where the aggregate loan does not exceed Rs. 20,000 or the loan is for the treatment of specified diseases. The perquisite, where taxable, is calculated at the rate prescribed in the Income-tax Rules and included in salary.
19.4 Recovery on exit. Any outstanding loan or advance is recovered from the full and final settlement. Where the settlement is insufficient, the Employee repays the balance before the relieving letter is issued, or agrees a repayment schedule with Payroll.

21.1 Overpayments. Where an Employee is paid more than the amount due, for example because of a delayed Leave Without Pay input, Payroll informs the Employee of the amount and the reason, and recovers it from salary in instalments not exceeding 25 per cent of the monthly net pay, unless the Employee chooses to repay it earlier.
21.2 Underpayments. Any underpayment is paid as arrears in the next payroll after it is identified, without the Employee having to apply.

22. COMPENSATION GOVERNANCE
22.1 Approvals. The pay ranges, the salary structure, the Target Variable Pay percentages and the annual increase budget are approved by the Chief People Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, and noted by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee of the Board. The pay of Employees in Grade L8 who are key managerial personnel is approved by the Committee and, where required by law, by the Board and the shareholders.
22.2 Exceptions. Any exception to this Policy for an individual, such as pay above the range maximum, a retention bonus above Rs. 10,00,000, or a variation of variable pay terms, requires the written approval of the Head, Total Rewards and the Chief People Officer, and is recorded in the exceptions register reviewed by Internal Audit each year.
22.3 Data and audit. Payroll data is processed in the payroll system with access restricted to Payroll and Total Rewards staff, and is audited each year by Internal Audit and the statutory auditors. Changes to an Employee's pay are made only on the basis of an approved record on the NPP, and every change is logged.

23. SUPPORT FOR DISABILITY
23.1 Dependent children with disabilities. A child with a disability of 40 per cent or more, certified by a competent medical authority, remains covered under the family floater of the group medical insurance without any age limit, whereas other children are covered up to the age of 25 years. The certificate is uploaded on the NPP at the time of enrolment or renewal.
23.2 Assistive devices and accessibility. The cost of assistive devices and software needed by an Employee with a disability to perform the role, such as screen readers, hearing aids used at work and adapted furniture, is borne by the Company outside CTC, on the recommendation of the HR Business Partner under the reasonable accommodation process in the Employee Handbook.
23.3 Transport allowance. An Employee with a locomotor or visual disability who does not use Company transport receives a transport allowance of Rs. 3,200 a month in addition to Annual Fixed Pay. The tax treatment of this allowance depends on the tax regime chosen.

text:
ANNEXURE B: GRATUITY ILLUSTRATIONS
B.1 Resignation after seven years and eight months. An Employee with a last drawn Basic Salary of Rs. 60,000 a month resigns after 7 years and 8 months of continuous service. The part-year of 8 months exceeds six months and is counted as a full year, giving 8 years. Gratuity is Rs. 60,000 multiplied by 15, divided by 26, multiplied by 8, which is Rs. 2,76,923, payable within 30 days of the last day of service.
B.2 Resignation after four years and ten months. An Employee resigns after 4 years and 10 months. The Employee has not completed five years of continuous service, so no gratuity is payable on resignation. The rounding of part-years in Clause 7.2 applies only to the calculation of the amount, not to the five-year condition for eligibility.
B.3 Death in service after three years. An Employee dies after 3 years and 2 months of service with a last drawn Basic Salary of Rs. 50,000. The five-year condition does not apply on death, so gratuity for 3 years is paid to the nominee: Rs. 50,000 multiplied by 15, divided by 26, multiplied by 3, which is Rs. 86,538.

ANNEXURE C: VARIABLE PAY ILLUSTRATIONS AND FREQUENTLY ASKED
QUESTIONS
C.1 How is my variable pay calculated? An Employee in Grade L5 has Annual Fixed Pay of Rs. 20,00,000, so Target Variable Pay at 12 per cent is Rs. 2,40,000. For a year with a Company Factor of 0.9 and a rating of 4 (Individual Factor 1.2), variable pay is Rs. 2,40,000 multiplied by 0.9 and 1.2, which is Rs. 2,59,200. If the Employee had joined on 1 July, nine complete months of service would give Rs. 1,94,400.
C.2 I resigned in May. Will I receive variable pay in June for the year that ended in March? No. Under Clause 8.4, an Employee who has resigned on or before the Payout Date is not eligible, even though the Performance Year was completed. The exceptions in Clause 8.5 cover death, permanent disability, retirement and termination by the Company for reasons other than misconduct or performance; they do not cover resignation.

C.3 I live in Bengaluru. Can I claim HRA exemption at 50 per cent? No. For HRA exemption, only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai are Metro Cities under Clause 2.6, so the limit for an Employee paying rent in Bengaluru is 40 per cent of Basic Salary. The HRA itself is paid at 50 per cent of Basic Salary at every location; only the tax exemption differs.

C.6 Can I opt out of provident fund because I want a higher take-home salary? C.11 I was on maternity leave for six months. Will my variable pay be reduced? No. Periods of maternity, adoption and paternity leave count as service for proration under Clause 8.3, and the rating is based on the period actually worked, as provided in the Leave Policy.
C.12 My sum insured was used up in the middle of the year. Is there any further cover? The family floater is shared by all members in the policy year. Where the sum insured is exhausted, further expenses are covered only by an optional top-up bought under Clause 9.3, or by the Employee's own insurance. The HR Helpdesk can advise on a corporate buffer, which the Chief People Officer may approve in exceptional cases.
C.13 Why does my CTC differ from the total of my twelve payslips? CTC includes the employer's provident fund contribution, the gratuity provision and Target Variable Pay, none of which appear as monthly earnings on the payslip. Variable pay is paid once a year in June, and gratuity only when employment ends after the qualifying period.
C.14 Does the Company pay statutory bonus to me? Only if the Employee's salary or wage, as defined in the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, is within the eligibility limit in Clause 15.1. Most Employees earn above the limit and receive variable pay instead.

ANNEXURE D: SUMMARY OF STATUTORY BENEFITS
The table below summarises the statutory benefits described in this Policy and the Company's practice where it goes beyond the law. The governing clause should be read for the complete rule.

Benefit: Provident fund | Who is covered: All Employees | Statutory position: 12 per cent employee and employer contribution | Company practice: Employer contribution on actual Basic Salary, not restricted to the wage ceiling

Benefit: Gratuity | Who is covered: Five years' continuous service, or death or disablement | Statutory position: Fifteen days' wages per year, subject to the ceiling; paid within 30 days | Company practice: Paid within 30 days irrespective of the settlement date
Benefit: Statutory bonus | Who is covered: Salary or wage up to the eligibility limit | Statutory position: 8.33 to 20 per cent | Company practice: Paid in addition to variable pay
Benefit: Maternity benefit | Who is covered: Women meeting the eligibility condition | Statutory position: Up to 26 weeks' paid leave | Company practice: Full salary paid; ESI benefit topped up

ANNEXURE F: TAX TREATMENT OF PAY COMPONENTS
The table below is a general guide to the income tax treatment of each component as applied by Payroll. Tax law changes each year and the individual position depends on the regime chosen; Employees should consult their own tax advisor.
Table 11: Tax treatment of pay components
Component: Basic Salary, special allowance, communication allowance | Old tax regime: Taxable | New tax regime: Taxable
Component: House rent allowance | Old tax regime: Partly exempt, as computed under the HRA rules | New tax regime: Fully taxable
Component: Leave travel allowance | Old tax regime: Exempt for eligible journeys, two in a block of four years | New tax regime: Fully taxable
Component: Meal card | Old tax regime: Exempt within the per-meal limit | New tax regime: Treated as per the rules applicable to the regime
Component: Employer provident fund contribution | Old tax regime: Not taxable up to the prescribed limit | New tax regime: Not taxable up to the prescribed limit
Component: Employer NPS contribution | Old tax regime: Deductible within the limit | New tax regime: Deductible within the limit
Component: Variable pay, awards, joining and retention bonus | Old tax regime: Taxable in the year paid | New tax regime: Taxable in the year paid
Component: ESOP exercise | Old tax regime: Perquisite on exercise | New tax regime: Perquisite on exercise
Component: Gratuity on leaving | Old tax regime: Exempt up to the statutory limit | New tax regime: Exempt up to the statutory limit
Component: Leave encashment on separation | Old tax regime: Exempt up to the notified limit | New tax regime: Exempt up to the notified limit

text:
CIRCULAR NO. HR/CIR/2025/03
Circular No.: HR/CIR/2025/03
Date of Issue: 2025-03-10
Effective From: 2025-04-01
Subject: Extension of employer NPS contribution to Grades L3 and L4
Amends: Clause 11.1, Table 1
Issued By: Chief People Officer and Chief Financial Officer
With effect from 1 April 2025, the option of an employer contribution to the National Pension System under Clause 11.1 is extended to Employees in Grades L3 and L4, on the same terms as for Grades L5 to L8. Employees in Grades L1 and L2 remain ineligible. Table 1 stands amended accordingly.

title: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
text:
1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND APPLICABLE LAW
1.1 Purpose. This Policy sets out the working hours of the Company, how attendance is recorded, the rules for Hybrid Work, shifts and on-call support, the payment of Overtime, and the transport and safety arrangements for Employees who work early or late.
1.2 Scope. This Policy applies to every Employee in Grades L1 to L8. Leave is governed by the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001). Where an Employee is deployed at a client site, the client's working hours apply where the Company has agreed to them, but the limits and payments in this Policy continue to apply.
1.3 Applicable law. Working hours, rest intervals, Overtime and the employment of women at night are regulated by the Shops and Establishments legislation of each State, listed in the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001). Notwithstanding anything in this Policy, where the law of the State in which the Employee works provides a limit or a payment more favourable to the Employee, the law prevails. In particular, the Shops and Establishments legislation of the States in which the Company operates requires Overtime to be paid at twice the ordinary rate of wages, and that rate applies wherever it exceeds the rate in this Policy.

text:
2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Base Location" means the office of the Company to which the Employee is attached, as recorded on the
NPP.
2.2 "Core Hours" means 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on a Working Day, in the time zone of the Base Location, during which every Employee on the general shift is expected to be available.
2.3 "Hybrid Work" means an arrangement under which an Employee works on some Working Days from the Base Location and on others from home, as approved under Section 5.
2.4 "Night Shift" means any shift that ends after 10:00 p.m. or begins before 6:00 a.m.
2.5 "Ordinary Rate of Wages" means the Employee's monthly Basic Salary and allowances forming part of Annual Fixed Pay, excluding variable pay, bonus and Overtime payments, divided by 26 for a daily rate and further divided by 8 for an hourly rate.
2.6 "Overtime" means work performed at the direction of the Reporting Manager in excess of nine hours in a day or 48 hours in a week, excluding the rest interval.
2.7 "Remote Work Day" means a Working Day on which the Employee works from home under an approved Hybrid Work arrangement.
2.8 "Working Day" has the meaning given in the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001), namely a day from Monday to Friday that is not a declared holiday for the Base Location.

title: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
text:
3. WORKING HOURS
3.1 Standard workday. The standard workday on the general shift is nine hours, including a rest interval of one hour, on each Working Day, giving about 45 hours of presence and 40 hours of work in a week. Within this, an Employee may choose the start time between 8:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m., provided the Core Hours are covered.
3.2 Statutory limits. No Employee is required to work more than nine hours in a day or 48 hours in a week, excluding Overtime permitted under Section 9, or to work for more than five hours continuously without a rest interval of at least half an hour. The spread-over of a workday, including rest intervals, does not exceed the limit prescribed by the law of the State.
3.3 Weekly off. Saturday and Sunday are weekly offs for the general shift. An Employee on a shift roster that includes a Saturday or Sunday receives two other days as weekly offs in the same week, recorded on the roster.
3.4 Workload. Reporting Managers plan work so that Employees are not routinely required to work beyond the standard workday. Sustained long hours are reviewed by the HR Business Partner, who may require additional staffing or a change in the plan.

title: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
text:
4. RECORDING ATTENDANCE
4.1 How attendance is recorded. On days worked at an office, attendance is recorded by the identity card at the entry gates; entry and exit times are transferred to the NPP daily. On a Remote Work Day, the Employee marks attendance on the NPP before 11:00 a.m. At a client site, the Employee marks attendance on the NPP and the Reporting Manager confirms it weekly.
4.2 Full and half days. A day with at least eight hours of presence at the office, or on which attendance has been marked on a Remote Work Day, is a full day. A day with at least four and a half but less than eight hours of presence is a half day, and the remaining half is debited to leave or, if no leave is applied for within three Working Days, treated as Leave Without Pay. Less than four and a half hours is treated as absence unless regularised.

text:
4.3 Regularisation. An Employee who forgot the identity card, was on official duty outside the office, or has an incorrect record may regularise attendance on the NPP, with the approval of the Reporting Manager, up to three times in a calendar month and within seven days of the date concerned. Regularisation for official duty, such as a client visit recorded on the NPP, does not count towards the limit.
4.4 Unauthorised absence. Absence without leave or regularisation is treated as Leave Without Pay, and continued absence is dealt with under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001) and the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).
4.5 Integrity of records. Marking attendance for another Employee, allowing another person to use one's identity card, or marking attendance on a Remote Work Day without working is falsification of records and is major misconduct under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).

title: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
text:
5. HYBRID WORK
5.1 Eligibility. Hybrid Work is available to an Employee whose role can be performed remotely without affecting client commitments or information security, as confirmed by the Reporting Manager. It is not available to Graduate Engineer Trainees during the training programme, to an Employee during the first four weeks after joining, or to an Employee on a performance improvement plan unless the plan provides otherwise.
5.2 Number of Remote Work Days. An eligible Employee may work from home for up to two Working Days in a week. The days are agreed between the Employee and the Reporting Manager, may differ between members of a team, and are recorded on the NPP at least one week in advance. Remote Work Days cannot be accumulated or carried to another week.
5.3 Conditions. On a Remote Work Day the Employee is available during Core Hours on the approved chat and telephone, attends scheduled meetings with the camera available when requested, uses only the Company laptop and virtual private network, works from a place where confidential information cannot be seen or heard by others, and complies with the IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
(NTL/HR/POL/009).

text:
6. SHIFTS AND SHIFT ALLOWANCE
6.1 Shift rosters. Employees supporting clients in other time zones may be placed on a shift roster, published on the NPP at least one week in advance. An Employee is not placed on a Night Shift for more than four consecutive weeks without a change to a day shift for at least one week, unless the Employee requests otherwise in writing.
6.2 Shift allowance. Employees in Grades L1 to L5 receive a shift allowance for each day worked on a shift other than the general shift, at the rates in Table 1. Employees in Grades L6 to L8 are not eligible for shift allowance, as their pay takes account of such work. Shift allowance is paid with the salary of the following month and is taxable.
6.3 On-call support. An Employee in Grades L1 to L5 who is designated on-call for a week, available by telephone outside working hours to respond to incidents, receives an on-call allowance of Rs. 1,500 for that week. Time spent actually working on an incident outside the shift is recorded on the NPP and, for Employees in Grades L1 to L3, counts towards Overtime.

section_title: Night Work and Safety of Women Employees
text:
7. NIGHT WORK AND SAFETY OF WOMEN EMPLOYEES
7.1 Consent. No woman Employee is required to work on a Night Shift without her written consent, given in the form in Annexure B. Consent may be withdrawn with two weeks' notice, and a woman Employee who declines or withdraws consent suffers no adverse consequence.
7.2 Safeguards. Where a woman Employee works on a Night Shift, the Company provides the safeguards required by the Shops and Establishments legislation of the State and the conditions of the Company's registration, which include at a minimum: (a) transport from the office to the residence and back, in a Company-arranged vehicle fitted with GPS tracking; (b) a security guard in the vehicle where a woman Employee is the first to be picked up or the last to be dropped, and the driver's and guard's verification by the police; (c) adequate lighting, security and a separate rest room at the office; and (d) a helpline monitored by the transport desk until every Employee on the Night Shift has reached home.
7.3 Reporting incidents. Any incident or concern during Company transport is reported immediately to the transport desk helpline, which escalates it to Security and the HR Business Partner. Misconduct by a driver or guard results in removal from Company duty.

title: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
text:
9. OVERTIME
9.1 Eligibility. Overtime is payable only to Employees in Grades L1 to L3. Employees in Grades L4 to L8 hold positions of supervision, management or specialised responsibility, and their pay takes account of occasional additional hours; they are not paid for Overtime but may receive compensatory off where eligible under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001).
9.2 Prior approval. Overtime is worked only at the written direction of the Reporting Manager recorded on the NPP before the work is done, except in an emergency, where it is recorded within one Working Day. Additional hours worked without direction are not Overtime.
9.3 Rate. Overtime is paid at one and a half times the Ordinary Rate of Wages for each hour of Overtime, rounded to the nearest half hour, with the salary of the following month.

title: Attendance, Hybrid Work and Overtime Policy
text:
9.4 Limits. Total Overtime for an Employee shall not exceed the quarterly limit prescribed by the law of the State, and in any case shall not exceed 50 hours in a calendar quarter. The Reporting Manager monitors the limit on the NPP, which blocks further Overtime once the limit is reached.
9.5 Overtime or compensatory off, not both. For the same hours of work on a weekly off or holiday, an Employee receives either Overtime payment or compensatory off under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001), but not both. The Employee chooses on the NPP when the work is recorded.
9.6 Illustration. An Employee in Grade L2 with Annual Fixed Pay of Rs. 6,24,000 has monthly fixed pay of Rs. 52,000, a daily rate of Rs. 2,000 and an hourly Ordinary Rate of Wages of Rs. 250. For six hours of approved Overtime in a month, the amount under Clause 9.3 is Rs. 250 multiplied by 1.5 and by 6, which is Rs. 2,250.

10.1 Statutory registers. HR Operations maintains, in electronic form on the NPP, the registers of attendance, working hours, Overtime and wages required by the Shops and Establishments legislation of each State, and produces them to an inspector on request.

11. TRAVEL TIME
11.1 Travel on a Working Day. Time spent travelling on Company business during a Working Day counts as working time. Where business travel extends the day beyond the standard workday, the extra time is not Overtime, but the Reporting Manager may allow a later start on the following day.
11.2 Travel on a weekly off or holiday. Where an Employee is required to travel on a weekly off or declared holiday to reach a client location, an Employee in Grades L1 to L4 is entitled to compensatory off for the day under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001). Travel on a weekly off at the Employee's own choice, for example to extend a stay, does not qualify.
11.3 Attendance while travelling. Days of business travel approved on the NPP are recorded as on duty and do not need regularisation.

text:
12. BREAKS, WELLBEING AND DISCONNECTING
12.1 Breaks. In addition to the one-hour rest interval, Employees may take short breaks during the day. Employees who work at a screen for long periods are encouraged to take a five-minute break every hour, and the ergonomic guidance on the NPP applies at home and in the office.
12.2 Nursing breaks. A woman Employee returning from maternity leave is entitled, until the child attains the age of fifteen months, to two breaks a day of the prescribed duration for nursing the child, in addition to the rest interval. On a Remote Work Day the breaks are taken at home; at the office the Employee may use the lactation room or the creche, as described in the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002).
12.3 Disconnecting after hours. Except for Employees on shift, on call or handling a declared incident, no Employee is expected to respond to non-urgent calls or messages between 8:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. or on weekly offs, as set out in the Employee Handbook. Reporting Managers who repeatedly contact team members outside these hours for non-urgent work are counselled by the HR Business Partner.

13. ATTENDANCE IN SPECIAL SITUATIONS
13.1 Bandh, strike or civil disturbance. Where a bandh, strike or civil disturbance is announced in a city, the location Crisis Management Team decides by 6:00 a.m. whether the office is open. Employees who can work from home do so, and the day is recorded as a Remote Work Day that does not count towards the weekly limit in Clause 5.2. Employees who cannot work are granted special leave as provided in the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001).
13.2 Polling day. On the day of a Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assembly election in the constituency where an Employee is registered, the Employee receives a paid holiday under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001). An Employee who must work on that day for a critical client commitment is given sufficient time off to vote.

13.3 Medical appointments. An Employee may attend a medical appointment during working hours by recording a half day of Sick Leave, or, for an appointment of less than two hours, by agreeing a later start or an earlier finish with the Reporting Manager and completing the Core Hours.
13.4 Religious observance. Reporting Managers accommodate reasonable requests to adjust working hours for religious observance, such as prayer times or fasting, provided that the Core Hours and client commitments are met. Requests are not refused on the ground of the religion concerned.
13.5 Attendance at a client site or abroad. An Employee deployed at a client site in India follows the client's workdays, but a Saturday or Sunday worked at the client's request is treated as a weekly off worked for the purposes of compensatory off and Overtime. ANNEXURE C: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
C.1 I came to office for six hours and then worked from home. How is the day recorded? Office presence of six hours is a half day under Clause 4.2. If the Reporting Manager agreed to the split day, the Employee regularises the day as a full day; this counts towards the three regularisations allowed in a month.
C.2 Can I carry forward an unused Remote Work Day to next week? No. Remote Work Days cannot be accumulated or carried forward under Clause 5.2.
C.3 I am an L4 and worked 12 hours on a release day. Do I get Overtime? No. Overtime is payable only to Grades L1 to L3 under Clause 9.1. An Employee in Grade L4 may be eligible for compensatory off only if the work was on a weekly off or holiday, as provided in the Leave Policy.

text:
CIRCULAR NO. HR/CIR/2025/10
Circular No.: HR/CIR/2025/10
Date of Issue: 2025-09-01
Effective From: 2025-10-01
Subject: Anchor days for office attendance
Amends: Clause 5.2
Issued By: Chief People Officer
To strengthen collaboration, with effect from 1 October 2025, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday are anchor days on which every Employee in Grades L1 to L6 on Hybrid Work attends the Base Location. Remote Work Days under Clause 5.2 may therefore be taken only on Monday and Friday, and the choice of days by agreement with the Reporting Manager no longer applies to Grades L1 to L6. (a) Employees in Grades L7 and L8 continue to agree their Remote Work Days with their Reporting Manager, within the limit of two days a week. (b) Where an anchor day is a declared holiday, the Employee is not required to attend on another day in its place. (c) Exceptions for medical reasons, disability or caregiving are approved by the HR Business Partner and recorded on the NPP.

CIRCULAR NO. HR/CIR/2025/10
Circular No.: HR/CIR/2025/10
Date of Issue: 2025-09-01
Effective From: 2025-10-01
Subject: Anchor days for office attendance
Amends: Clause 5.2
Issued By: Chief People Officer
To strengthen collaboration, with effect from 1 October 2025, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday are anchor days on which every Employee in Grades L1 to L6 on Hybrid Work attends the Base Location. Remote Work Days under Clause 5.2 may therefore be taken only on Monday and Friday, and the choice of days by agreement with the Reporting Manager no longer applies to Grades L1 to L6. (a) Employees in Grades L7 and L8 continue to agree their Remote Work Days with their Reporting Manager, within the limit of two days a week. (b) Where an anchor day is a declared holiday, the Employee is not required to attend on another day in its place. (c) Exceptions for medical reasons, disability or caregiving are approved by the HR Business Partner and recorded on the NPP.

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
1.1 Purpose. This Policy sets out how Business Travel is approved and booked, the class of travel, hotel and daily allowances to which Employees are entitled by Grade, and how expenses are claimed and reimbursed. It aims to ensure that Employees travel safely and in reasonable comfort, and that the Company's money is spent prudently.
1.2 Scope. This Policy covers domestic and international Business Travel, local conveyance on Company business, and other business expenses such as client entertainment approved under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004). Relocation on transfer is governed by the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002), and assignments abroad of more than 90 days by the assignment letter.
1.3 Client-billable travel. Where travel is billable to a client, the client's travel policy applies if it is more restrictive than this Policy and the Company has agreed to it. The project manager informs the Employee of any such restriction before the travel is booked.

text:
2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Base Location" means the office to which the Employee is attached, as recorded on the NPP.
2.2 "Business Travel" means travel away from the Base Location on the Company's business, approved on the NPP before the journey, and includes travel to a client site, another Company office, a training programme or a conference.
2.3 "Metro City" means, for the purposes of this Policy only, Mumbai, Delhi and the National Capital Region (including Noida, Gurugram, Ghaziabad and Faridabad), Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Pune. All other cities in India are non-metro cities for hotel limits. This definition does not apply to the income tax exemption for house rent allowance, for which the Compensation and Benefits Policy (NTL/HR/POL/005) uses a different list.
2.4 "Per Diem" means the fixed daily allowance paid for each day of Business Travel to cover meals, laundry, tips and incidental expenses, without the need to produce bills.
2.5 "Travel Desk" means the team in Finance Operations, together with the Company's appointed travel agency, that books tickets, hotels and transfers for Business Travel.

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
3. APPROVAL AND BOOKING
3.1 Travel request. Every Business Travel is requested on the NPP, stating the purpose, dates, destination and cost centre, and approved before any booking is made. Domestic travel is approved by the Reporting Manager. International travel is approved by the Reporting Manager and the Business Unit Head. Travel billable to a client also requires the client's approval where the contract so provides.
3.2 Booking through the Travel Desk. Tickets, hotels and airport transfers are booked by the Travel Desk on the basis of the approved request. Domestic travel is requested at least seven days, and international travel at least 21 days, before the date of travel, so that economical fares can be obtained. Urgent travel at shorter notice is permitted when the reason is recorded on the request.

text:
3.3 Lowest logical fare. The Travel Desk books the lowest available fare on a direct or reasonably timed route within the class of travel entitled. An Employee who asks for a particular airline or time for personal convenience, where it costs more than the lowest logical fare by more than Rs. 2,000, bears the difference, unless the Reporting Manager approves it on the request.
3.4 Self-booking. An Employee may book travel personally only where the Travel Desk cannot be reached, such as outside its hours for an urgent trip, and must book within the entitlement at the lowest logical fare. The reason is recorded on the claim.
3.5 Changes and cancellations. Changes and cancellations are made through the Travel Desk as early as possible. Cancellation charges arising from a business reason are borne by the Company. Charges arising from a personal reason are borne by the Employee unless the Reporting Manager waives them, for example for a medical emergency.

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
4. CLASS OF TRAVEL
4.1 Entitlement by Grade. The class of travel for each Grade is set out in Table 1. An Employee may travel in a lower class than entitled but is not reimbursed the difference.
4.2 Short journeys for Grades L1 to L3. For journeys of 500 km or less, Employees in Grades L1 to L3 travel by rail in AC 3-tier or by air-conditioned bus. Air travel for such a journey may be approved by the Reporting Manager only where no suitable rail or bus connection allows the Employee to reach the destination in time, and the reason is recorded on the request.
4.3 Road travel. Travel between cities by a hired car is permitted for journeys of up to 300 km where it is cheaper or more practical than rail or air, or where three or more Employees travel together. Employees do not drive themselves on journeys of more than 250 km without the Reporting Manager's approval, as required by the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
7. LOCAL CONVEYANCE AND AIRPORT TRANSFERS
7.1 Airport and station transfers. Transfers between the residence or hotel and the airport or railway station are reimbursed as follows: (a) Employees in Grades L4 and L5 may use an app-based cab in the standard category, or a prepaid taxi, and claim the actual fare; (b) Employees in Grades L6 to L8 may use an app-based cab in the premium sedan category and claim the actual fare; and (c) Employees in Grades L1 to L3 use the airport bus, metro rail or a shared or pooled cab, and are reimbursed the actual fare up to Rs. 750 for each trip.
7.2 Local travel at the destination. Travel between the hotel and the client site or Company office at the destination is reimbursed at the actual fare of public transport or an app-based cab in the standard category, for all Grades. The Travel Desk may arrange a shared car for a team at the same site.

8. INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL
8.1 Documents. The Employee holds a passport valid for at least six months beyond the return date. The Travel Desk arranges the visa through the Company's immigration partner on the basis of the approved request and the invitation letter; the Employee provides documents promptly. Unspent balances are returned within 15 days of return. Purchases of foreign exchange are made through the Travel Desk within the limits applicable to business travel under the foreign exchange regulations.
8.3 Insurance. Every Employee on international Business Travel is covered by the Company's overseas travel insurance for medical expenses, evacuation, loss of passport and baggage delay. The policy details and the 24-hour assistance number are sent with the itinerary.
8.4 High-risk destinations. Travel to a country or region that the Company's security advisor rates as high risk requires the prior approval of the Chief People Officer and a security briefing. The Company may require the Employee to leave such a destination at short notice.

text:
9. CLAIMS AND REIMBURSEMENT
9.1 Submitting a claim. Expenses are claimed on the NPP within 30 days of the end of the trip, or of the date of the expense for local claims, with scanned receipts attached. Claims submitted after 30 days require the Business Unit Head's approval, and claims submitted after 90 days are not reimbursed.
9.2 Receipts. Receipts are required for every expense above Rs. 500, other than the Per Diem and the lodging allowance. Where a receipt is lost, the Employee submits a declaration on the NPP explaining the expense; declarations are accepted for up to Rs. 2,000 in a trip and are reviewed by Internal Audit.
9.3 Approval and payment. Claims are approved by the Reporting Manager within five Working Days and checked by Finance Operations. Approved claims are reimbursed with the next monthly salary, or, where the amount exceeds Rs. 25,000, by separate bank transfer within ten Working Days of approval.
9.4 Audit. Finance Operations audits a sample of claims every month and all claims above Rs. 50,000. Employees keep original receipts for six months after reimbursement and produce them on request.

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
10. TAX AND ADVANCES
10.1 Tax treatment. Reimbursement of actual expenses incurred on Business Travel, and the Per Diem within the rates in this Policy, are treated as business expenses of the Company and are not taxable in the hands of the Employee. Amounts reimbursed that are not for Business Travel, or allowances paid without travel, are added to salary and tax is deducted at source.
10.2 Travel advance. An Employee may request a travel advance on the NPP of up to the Per Diem for the days of travel plus 50 per cent, for trips where the hotel and tickets are not paid directly by the Company. The advance is settled by a claim within 15 days of return; an advance not settled within 30 days is recovered from the next salary.
10.3 Corporate card. Employees in Grades L6 to L8 who travel frequently may be issued a corporate card for business expenses. Card statements are reconciled with claims on the NPP each month; personal use of the corporate card is not permitted.

text:
11. SAFETY AND WELLBEING ON TRAVEL
11.1 Itinerary and contact. Every itinerary is recorded on the NPP so that the Travel Desk can locate Employees in an emergency. Employees keep their mobile phones reachable and inform the Travel Desk of any change in plans.
11.2 Late arrivals. Where an Employee arrives at a destination between 9:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m., the Travel Desk arranges a pre-booked transfer from the airport or station to the hotel, and the hotel is informed of the late check-in. Employees arriving late are not expected to use public transport.
11.3 Rest after long journeys. An Employee arriving after an overnight flight of more than eight hours is not expected to work for the rest of that day, and a Reporting Manager does not schedule client meetings within six hours of such an arrival, except in an emergency.

text:
16. ACCESSIBILITY, HEALTH AND SUSTAINABLE TRAVEL
16.1 Employees with disabilities. An Employee with a disability may travel in a higher class, choose an accessible hotel outside the approved list, and be accompanied by an escort whose travel and stay are paid by the Company, where the HR Business Partner confirms that this is needed. The Travel Desk records the requirements on the Employee's profile so that they are applied automatically.
16.2 Pregnancy. A pregnant Employee may decline Business Travel without any adverse consequence. Air travel after 28 weeks of pregnancy requires a fitness-to-fly certificate, in line with airline requirements, and the Travel Desk books aisle seats close to the front of the aircraft on request.
16.3 Sustainable travel. Employees consider whether a meeting can be held by video before requesting travel. For journeys of up to 300 km, rail or road is preferred to air where the travel time is reasonable. The Travel Desk reports the estimated carbon emissions of each business unit's travel every quarter.

C.4 Worked example of a domestic claim. An Employee in Grade L5 travels from Pune to Hyderabad for three days and two nights; the Travel Desk books the flights and the hotel. The Employee claims three days of Per Diem at Rs. 1,000, which is Rs. 3,000; airport transfers of Rs. 650 and Rs. 720 at Pune and Rs. 840 and Rs. 910 at Hyderabad, which is Rs. 3,120; and local cabs to the client site of Rs. 1,160. The total claim is Rs. 7,280, with receipts attached for the four transfers and the cab trips above Rs. 500.

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
C.5 The client is providing lunch and dinner at the workshop. Do I still get the Per Diem? Yes, but reduced by 50 per cent for each day on which lunch and dinner are provided, under Clause 6.2.
C.6 Can I claim a dinner with a client as an L3? No. Under Clause 13.1, only Employees in Grades L4 to L8 host client entertainment. An Employee in Grade L3 may attend a meal hosted by a colleague in an eligible Grade.
C.7 My trip was cancelled by the client after booking. Who pays the cancellation charge? The Company, because the cancellation arose from a business reason under Clause 3.5. The Travel Desk records the reason on the request.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND PRECEDENCE
1.1 Purpose. This Policy sets out how employment with the Company ends, the Notice Periods that apply, the exit process and clearances, the Full and Final Settlement, the documents issued to a departing Employee, and the obligations that continue after employment ends. It aims to make every exit orderly, fair and respectful.
1.2 Scope. This Policy applies to every Employee in Grades L1 to L8, whether the separation is by resignation, termination, retirement, death, Absconding or the end of a fixed-term contract.
1.3 Precedence. This Policy governs Notice Periods and the exit process. Where the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002) summarises Notice Periods differently, this Policy prevails. Payments that form part of the settlement are calculated in accordance with the policy governing each payment, and where a statute provides a more favourable time limit or amount, the statute prevails.

text:
2. DEFINITIONS
2.1 "Absconding" means absence from duty without sanctioned leave and without intimation for eight or more consecutive Working Days, as described in Section 11.
2.2 "Full and Final Settlement" (F&F) means the final statement of all amounts payable to and recoverable from a departing Employee, and the payment or recovery of the net amount.
2.3 "Garden Leave" means a period of the Notice Period during which the Employee remains employed and paid but is not required or permitted to work or to access Company systems and premises.
2.4 "Last Day of Service" means the last day on which the Employee is on the rolls of the Company, as recorded on the NPP.
2.5 "Notice Pay" means the monthly fixed pay of the Employee divided by 30, multiplied by the number of days concerned.
2.6 "Notice Period" means the period of notice set out in Table 1 for the Employee's Grade, counted in calendar days from the day after the resignation or the notice of termination is recorded on the NPP.
2.7 "Relieving Letter" means the letter confirming that the Employee has been relieved of duties and has completed exit clearances, stating the date of joining, the Last Day of Service and the last designation.
2.8 "Working Day" has the meaning given in the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001).

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
3. WAYS IN WHICH EMPLOYMENT ENDS
3.1 Modes of separation. Employment ends by resignation by the Employee; termination by the Company on grounds of performance, misconduct or redundancy; retirement on superannuation; death; Absconding; or the end of a fixed-term contract. The process for each is described in this Policy.
3.2 Fixed-term contracts. A fixed-term contract ends on the date stated in it without notice, unless it is extended or converted in writing before that date. An Employee on a fixed-term contract who wishes to leave before that date gives the Notice Period for the Grade.
3.3 Respectful exits. Every separation, whatever its reason, is handled confidentially and with courtesy. Information about the reason for an Employee's exit is shared only with those who need it.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
4. RESIGNATION
4.1 How to resign. An Employee resigns by submitting a resignation on the NPP, which records the date and time. A resignation by e-mail or letter is accepted only where the NPP is unavailable and is recorded on the NPP by the HR Business Partner within one Working Day.
4.2 Acknowledgement and discussion. The Reporting Manager acknowledges the resignation on the NPP within two Working Days and may hold a conversation with the Employee to understand the reasons. No Employee is pressured to withdraw a resignation, and a resignation cannot be refused.
4.3 Withdrawal. An Employee may request to withdraw a resignation within seven days of submitting it. The withdrawal takes effect only if approved by the Reporting Manager and the HR Business Partner, who may decline it where a replacement has already been confirmed.
4.4 Last Day of Service. The Last Day of Service is the last day of the Notice Period, unless it is advanced under Clause 5.3 or Clause 5.4, or extended under the leave rules in Clause 5.6.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
5. NOTICE PERIOD
5.1 Notice by Grade. The Notice Period for resignation and for termination by the Company, other than for misconduct, is set out in Table 1. An Employee in Grades L5 to L8 serves a Notice Period of 90 days.
5.2 Notice during probation. A Probationer of any Grade, as defined in the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001), serves a Notice Period of 15 days, and the Company gives 15 days' notice or Notice Pay in lieu when ending employment during probation.
5.3 Waiver by the Company. The Company may, at its discretion, waive the whole or part of the Notice Period at the Employee's request, having regard to the handover of work and client commitments. A waiver is approved by the Reporting Manager and, for Grades L5 to L8, the Business Unit Head, and no recovery is made for the waived days.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
5.4 Buyout by the Employee. An Employee who wishes to leave before completing the Notice Period, and whose request for a waiver is not approved, may buy out the whole or any part of the unserved Notice Period by paying Notice Pay for the unserved days, with the approval of the Reporting Manager and the HR Business Partner. The amount is recovered from the F&F.
5.5 Unserved notice without buyout. Where an Employee leaves without serving the Notice Period and without an approved waiver or buyout, Notice Pay for the unserved days is recovered from the F&F, and the Relieving Letter is not issued until the recovery is complete. The service certificate is issued in any case.
5.6 Leave during the Notice Period. Leave during the Notice Period is governed by the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001). Leave other than certified Sick Leave extends the Last Day of Service by the number of days of leave, unless the Reporting Manager waives the extension.
5.7 Garden Leave. The Company may place an Employee on Garden Leave for the whole or part of the Notice Period, for example where the Employee is joining a competitor or has access to sensitive information. During Garden Leave, the Employee is paid in full and remains bound by all obligations of employment, including confidentiality and the prohibition on outside employment.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
6. TERMINATION BY THE COMPANY
6.1 Performance. Employment may be terminated for performance only after the Employee has been given a performance improvement plan under the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002), with specific goals and support, and has not met the goals. The Company gives the Notice Period for the Grade or Notice Pay in lieu.
6.2 Misconduct. Employment may be terminated for misconduct after the disciplinary procedure in the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004). Termination for gross misconduct is without notice or Notice Pay.
6.3 Redundancy. Where a role becomes redundant because of the loss of a client, a restructuring or a change in technology, the Company first seeks a suitable alternative role for the Employee for at least 30 days. If none is found, employment is terminated with the Notice Period or Notice Pay in lieu, and severance pay under Clause 6.4.

6. TERMINATION BY THE COMPANY
6.1 Performance. Employment may be terminated for performance only after the Employee has been given a performance improvement plan under the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002), with specific goals and support, and has not met the goals. The Company gives the Notice Period for the Grade or Notice Pay in lieu.
6.2 Misconduct. Employment may be terminated for misconduct after the disciplinary procedure in the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004). Termination for gross misconduct is without notice or Notice Pay.
6.3 Redundancy. Where a role becomes redundant because of the loss of a client, a restructuring or a change in technology, the Company first seeks a suitable alternative role for the Employee for at least 30 days. If none is found, employment is terminated with the Notice Period or Notice Pay in lieu, and severance pay under Clause 6.4.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
6.4 Severance pay. An Employee whose employment ends by redundancy receives severance pay of one month's fixed pay for each completed year of service, subject to a minimum of two months and a maximum of six months, in addition to Notice Pay. Where the Employee is a workman entitled to retrenchment compensation under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 or the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the severance pay includes that compensation and is never less than it.
6.5 Outplacement support. An Employee leaving by redundancy is offered three months of outplacement support from an external provider, continued group medical insurance for three months after the Last Day of Service, and a reference confirming that the separation was not related to performance or conduct.

title: Separation and Exit Policy

7.1 Handover. Within five Working Days of the resignation, the Employee and the Reporting Manager agree a handover plan on the NPP, listing work to be transferred, documents and credentials to be handed over, and client communication. The Reporting Manager confirms completion before the Last Day of Service.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
8. FULL AND FINAL SETTLEMENT
8.1 Components. The F&F includes the following, calculated in accordance with the policy governing each item: (a) fixed pay for the days worked up to the Last Day of Service; (b) encashment of the Earned Leave balance on the Last Day of Service, up to a maximum of 30 days, at Basic Salary divided by 26 for each day; (c) gratuity, where the Employee is eligible under the Compensation and Benefits Policy
(NTL/HR/POL/005);
(d) variable pay, where payable under the Compensation and Benefits Policy; (e) approved reimbursements and claims not yet paid; and (f) recoveries, including unserved Notice Pay, outstanding loans and advances, prorated joining or relocation bonus, and the value of unreturned assets.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
8.2 Time for settlement. The F&F is processed and the net amount paid within 45 days of the Last Day of Service, provided that all clearances have been completed. Gratuity, where payable, is paid together with the F&F within the same 45 days.
8.3 Statement and queries. The F&F statement is published on the NPP and sent to the Employee's personal e-mail address. The Employee may raise a query within 30 days of the statement; Payroll responds within ten Working Days and pays any correction within a further ten Working Days.
8.4 Net amount payable by the Employee. Where recoveries exceed the amounts payable, the Employee pays the difference within 30 days of the statement. The Relieving Letter is issued on payment.
8.5 Tax. Tax is deducted at source on the F&F in accordance with law, taking into account the exemptions for gratuity and leave encashment on separation. Form 16 for the year is issued after the end of the financial year.

9. RELIEVING LETTER AND OTHER DOCUMENTS
9.1 Relieving Letter and service certificate. The Relieving Letter and a service certificate stating the dates of employment and the last designation are issued within seven Working Days after all clearances are completed and any amount due from the Employee is paid. The service certificate does not comment on performance or the reason for leaving.
