9.3 References. Requests for references from prospective employers or background verification agencies are answered only by HR Operations and only with the Employee's consent, confirming the dates of employment, the last designation and the Grade. Managers do not give personal references on behalf of the Company.
9.4 Insurance continuation. Group medical insurance ends on the Last Day of Service, except as provided in Clause 6.5. The insurer's conversion option is described in the exit kit on the NPP.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
10. OBLIGATIONS AFTER EMPLOYMENT
10.1 Confidentiality. The obligation to keep confidential the information of the Company, its clients and its Employees continues after the Last Day of Service without limit of time. The Employee returns or destroys all confidential material and confirms this in the exit declaration.
10.2 Non-solicitation of Employees. For 12 months after the Last Day of Service, the former Employee shall not solicit or induce any Employee with whom the former Employee worked in the last 12 months of employment to leave the Company.
10.3 Non-solicitation of clients. For 12 months after the Last Day of Service, the former Employee shall not solicit business from, or provide services directly to, any client for whom the former Employee worked in the last 12 months of employment, in competition with the Company. Joining a client as its own employee is subject to the terms of the Company's contract with that client, which the HR Business Partner will explain.
10.4 No post-employment non-compete. The Company does not restrict a former Employee from joining a competitor after the Last Day of Service, recognising that agreements in restraint of trade after employment are generally void under Indian law. The obligations in Clause 10.1 to Clause 10.3 continue to apply.
10.5 Intellectual property. Work product created during employment remains the property of the Company or its client under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004). The former Employee assists, at the Company's cost, with any formality needed to record the Company's rights.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
11. ABSCONDING
11.1 Contacting the Employee. Where an Employee is absent without intimation, the Reporting Manager tries to contact the Employee and the emergency contact by telephone and e-mail on the first and third Working Days, and informs the HR Business Partner, who checks whether the Employee is safe.
11.2 Letters. Where the absence continues for eight consecutive Working Days, HR Operations sends a letter by registered post and e-mail to the last known addresses, asking the Employee to report or explain the absence within seven days. If there is no response, a second letter is sent giving a further seven days and stating that the Employee will otherwise be treated as having abandoned employment.
11.3 Deemed abandonment. If the Employee does not respond to the second letter, the Employee is treated as having abandoned employment with effect from the first day of absence. The F&F is prepared with recovery of Notice Pay for the Notice Period, only a service certificate stating the dates of employment is issued, and the separation is recorded as Absconding. The Company does not issue a Relieving Letter.
11.4 Return and explanation. Where the Employee reports or responds with an explanation, such as a medical emergency, the absence is dealt with under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001) and, where appropriate, the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
12. RETIREMENT, DEATH AND REHIRE
12.1 Retirement. Employees retire on the last day of the month in which they attain the age of 60 years. The Company may offer a retired Employee a fixed-term consultancy or contract where business needs require, on terms agreed at the time.
12.2 Death in service. On the death of an Employee in service, the HR Business Partner contacts the family to offer support and to guide them through the formalities. The F&F, gratuity, insurance and the family support described in the Compensation and Benefits Policy (NTL/HR/POL/005), and leave encashment under the Leave Policy (NTL/HR/POL/001), are paid to the nominee within 15 days of receiving the death certificate and the claim documents. No notice or recovery for unserved notice applies.
12.3 Rehire. A former Employee who left by resignation or redundancy may be rehired after six months from the Last Day of Service. A former Employee terminated for misconduct or recorded as Absconding is not eligible for rehire. On rehire within 12 months of the Last Day of Service, the previous service is counted for the long service awards in the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002).

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
13. SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES
13.1 During maternity leave. The Company does not terminate the employment of a woman Employee during her maternity leave, and a discharge or dismissal during maternity absence is unlawful except for gross misconduct in the circumstances permitted by the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961. A redundancy affecting her role is deferred until she has returned and been offered any suitable alternative role.
13.2 During illness. Employment is not terminated for performance while an Employee is on certified Sick Leave or special sick leave. Where an Employee is unable to return to work after prolonged illness, the HR Business Partner explores reasonable accommodation and alternative roles before any separation is considered, and any separation on medical grounds is approved by the Chief People Officer.
13.3 Resignation during a performance improvement plan. An Employee on a performance improvement plan may resign at any time. The plan ends on resignation, and the Notice Period applies in the usual way. The resignation does not affect the Employee's eligibility for rehire under Clause 12.3.
13.4 Resignation during an inquiry. Where an Employee resigns while a disciplinary inquiry or an Internal Committee inquiry is pending, the inquiry is completed and its outcome recorded. The Relieving Letter may be withheld until the outcome is known, but for not more than 60 days after the Last Day of Service, and the service certificate is issued in any case.

section_title: Exits From Client Sites and Assignments Abroad
text:
14. EXITS FROM CLIENT SITES AND ASSIGNMENTS ABROAD
14.1 Client access and assets. An Employee deployed at a client site returns the client's identity card, equipment and tokens to the client's project manager on or before the Last Day of Service, and the Reporting Manager confirms the return in the handover plan. The client's own exit formalities are completed where the contract requires them.
14.2 Assignments abroad. An Employee on an assignment abroad who resigns returns to India before the Last Day of Service unless the Business Unit Head approves otherwise. The Company bears the cost of the return journey, and host-country formalities, such as the cancellation of a work permit and final tax filings, are completed through the Company's advisors.
14.3 Visa sponsorship. Where the Company has sponsored a work visa, it informs the immigration authorities of the end of employment where the law of the host country requires, and the former Employee is responsible for complying with the conditions of the visa after the Last Day of Service.

16. APPEALS AND CONCERNS
16.1 Appeal against termination. An Employee whose employment is terminated for performance or redundancy may appeal in writing to the Chief People Officer within 15 days of the notice of termination. The Chief People Officer, or a senior leader nominated by the Chief People Officer who was not involved in the decision, decides within 30 days. Appeals against termination for misconduct follow the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).
16.2 Concerns about the settlement or documents. A concern about the Full and Final Settlement, the Relieving Letter or any other document is raised as a ticket through the HR Helpdesk and, if unresolved within ten Working Days, escalated to the Head, HR Operations.

title: Separation and Exit Policy
text:
ANNEXURE C: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
C.1 Can my manager refuse my resignation? No. A resignation cannot be refused under Clause 4.2. The manager may discuss the reasons, and the Company may decide whether to waive any part of the Notice Period.
C.2 I have an offer that needs me to join in 45 days, but my notice is 60 days. What can I do? Request a waiver of 15 days under Clause 5.3. If it is not approved, the unserved days may be bought out under Clause 5.4, subject to approval and to any circular limiting buyout.
C.3 Can I take my pending Earned Leave during notice instead of encashing it? Only with the approval of the Reporting Manager and the HR Business Partner, and such leave extends the Last Day of Service unless the extension is waived, as provided in the Leave Policy.

text:
C.4 When will I get my Relieving Letter? Within seven Working Days after clearances are complete and any amount due from you is paid, under Clause 9.1, subject to any circular that shortens this time.
C.5 I am joining a competitor. Will the Company stop me? No. There is no post-employment non-compete under Clause 10.4. The Company may place you on Garden Leave during the Notice Period, and your confidentiality and non-solicitation obligations continue after you leave.
C.6 I am on maternity leave and my project has been closed. Can I be let go? No. The Company does not terminate employment during maternity leave, and any redundancy is deferred until after return and after alternative roles have been considered, under Clause 13.1.

C.7 Can the Company withhold my Relieving Letter because an inquiry is pending? Only until the outcome is known and for not more than 60 days after the Last Day of Service, under Clause 13.4. The service certificate is issued in any case.
C.8 I was made redundant after four years. What will I receive? clause_title: Limit on buyout of the Notice Period
text:
CIRCULAR NO. HR/CIR/2025/04
Circular No.: HR/CIR/2025/04
Date of Issue: 2025-04-07
Effective From: 2025-04-15
Subject: Limit on buyout of the Notice Period
Amends: Clause 5.4
Issued By: Chief People Officer
To protect client delivery during transitions, with effect from 15 April 2025, an Employee may buy out not more than 50 per cent of the Notice Period under Clause 5.4. The balance must be served, unless it is waived by the Company under Clause 5.3. For example, an Employee in Grade L3 with a Notice Period of 60 days must serve at least 30 days, and may buy out up to 30 days. Buyout during probation is not affected.

title: IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
1. PURPOSE, SCOPE AND RESPONSIBILITIES
1.1 Purpose. The Company holds information entrusted to it by clients, Employees and partners. This Policy sets the rules for using the Company's information technology, for protecting information and personal data, and for reporting incidents, so that the Company meets its obligations under client contracts and applicable law and protects the people whose data it holds.
1.2 Scope. This Policy applies to every Employee, consultant and contractor who uses a Company device, a Company or client system, or a BYOD Device for work, at any location, including at home, at a client site and while travelling.
1.3 Client requirements. Where a client contract or the client's security policy imposes stricter requirements than this Policy for a project, the stricter requirements apply to that project. The project manager communicates them at onboarding, and they are recorded on the project's security plan.
1.4 Responsibilities. The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) owns this Policy and the security programme. The IT Service Desk provides devices, access and first-line support. The Security Operations Centre monitors systems and responds to incidents. The Data Protection Officer oversees compliance with data protection law. Every Employee is responsible for following this Policy and for reporting incidents promptly.

4. ACCEPTABLE USE
4.1 Business use. Company devices, networks, e-mail and systems are provided for the Company's business. Limited personal use, such as reading news or making a personal online payment, is permitted if it is occasional, does not interfere with work, does not consume significant resources, and does not breach this Policy.
4.2 Prohibited use. 4.3 No expectation of privacy on Company systems. Information created, stored or sent on Company systems belongs to the Company. Employees should not expect privacy in their use of Company systems, subject to the limits on monitoring in Section 13.

title: IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
5. ACCOUNTS, PASSWORDS AND ACCESS
5.1 Individual accounts. Each user has a unique account. Actions performed with an account are attributed to its holder. Shared or generic accounts are permitted only where approved by the CISO for a technical need, with a named owner.
5.2 Passwords. Passwords are at least 12 characters long, combine upper and lower case letters, numbers and symbols, are not reused across the last ten passwords, and are changed every 90 days. Passwords are never written down, shared or stored in a browser on a shared computer; the Company's password manager may be used.
5.3 Multi-Factor Authentication. Multi-Factor Authentication is mandatory for e-mail, the virtual private network, the NPP, cloud administration consoles and all client systems that support it. Employees never approve an authentication request they did not initiate, and report any unexpected request to the SOC immediately.
5.4 Access on the basis of need. Access to systems and data is granted on the basis of least privilege and approved by the Information Asset owner. Access is reviewed every quarter by the owner, and removed within one Working Day of a change of role or project and on the Last Day of Service.
5.5 Privileged access. Administrator and production access is granted only to named Employees for a defined need, through a separate privileged account with MFA, and every privileged session is logged. Production access for Client Data requires the client's approval where the contract so requires.

text:
6. COMPANY DEVICES
6.1 Standard controls. Company laptops are issued with full-disk encryption, endpoint detection and response software, the virtual private network client and data loss prevention controls. Screens lock automatically after five minutes of inactivity. Security updates are installed within seven days of release; a device that is not updated within 14 days is blocked from the network until it is.
6.2 Removable media. USB storage devices, memory cards and external drives are blocked on Company laptops. An exception for a specific business need, such as delivering a build to a client on encrypted media, requires the approval of the CISO and is time-limited.
6.3 Printing. Confidential and Restricted documents are printed only on Company printers using secure release with the identity card, and collected immediately. Printing Client Data at home or at a public printing shop is prohibited.
6.4 Loss or theft. The loss or theft of a Company device is reported to the SOC within one hour of discovery, so that the device can be locked and wiped remotely, and to the police as described in the Employee Handbook (NTL/HR/POL/002).

text:
8. E-MAIL, COLLABORATION AND INTERNET
8.1 Phishing. Employees are cautious with unexpected e-mails and messages, particularly those that ask for credentials, payment, urgent action or the opening of attachments. Suspicious e-mails are reported using the report button in the e-mail client. The Company runs simulated phishing exercises; an Employee who fails repeatedly is assigned additional training.
8.2 Sending information outside the Company. Confidential information sent outside the Company is encrypted using the Company's secure mail or file transfer tool. Automatic forwarding of Company e-mail to any external address is blocked. Restricted information is never sent by e-mail.
8.3 Collaboration tools. Only the Company's approved chat, video conferencing and file-sharing tools are used for work. Client-specific tools may be used where the client requires, through accounts provided by the client. Recording of meetings is governed by the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).
8.4 Internet access. Web filtering blocks categories of websites that present security or legal risk, including malware, gambling, adult content and unapproved file-sharing sites. An Employee who needs access to a blocked site for work requests it through the IT Service Desk.

9. CLIENT DATA AND CLIENT ENVIRONMENTS
9.1 Use only for the client. Client Data is used only for the project for which it was provided, is accessed only by Employees assigned to that project, and is never copied to Company systems outside the project environment, to another client's environment, or to any personal device or account.
9.2 Offshore development centres. Projects that require it are delivered from a secured offshore development centre with badge-controlled access limited to project members. In such areas, personal mobile phones, cameras and storage devices are deposited at the entrance, printing is disabled, and a clean desk is maintained at all times.

title: IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
11. PERSONAL DATA PROTECTION
11.1 Roles of the Company. For the Personal Data of its Employees and candidates, the Company is a data fiduciary under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. For Personal Data in Client Data, the Company usually processes it on behalf of the client, and follows the client's instructions and the contract.
11.2 Principles. The Company processes Personal Data only for a lawful purpose, on the basis of consent or a legitimate use permitted by law, with a clear notice to the Data Principal; collects only the data needed for the purpose; keeps it accurate; retains it only as long as needed under Table 3; and protects it with reasonable security safeguards as required by the Act.
11.3 Rights of Data Principals. Employees and candidates may exercise the rights given to Data Principals by the Act, including the right to access information about their Personal Data, to correction and erasure, to grievance redressal, and to nominate another person to exercise their rights in the event of death or incapacity, by writing to the Data Protection Officer at dpo@nexora.example. The Data Protection Officer responds within the time required by law and in any case within 30 days.
11.4 Personal Data Breach. In the event of a Personal Data Breach involving Personal Data for which the Company is the data fiduciary, the Company informs the Data Protection Board of India and each affected Data Principal in the form and manner prescribed under the Act. Where the Company processes the data for a client, it informs the client within the time required by the contract so that the client can meet its obligations.
11.5 Retention. Personal Data held by the Company about Employees and candidates is retained for the periods in Table 3, and then deleted or anonymised, unless a longer period is required by law or for a pending legal proceeding.

title: IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
12. SECURITY INCIDENTS
12.1 Report immediately. Every Employee reports a known or suspected Security Incident to the SOC immediately and in any case within one hour of becoming aware of it, by telephone on the security hotline or by e-mail to itsd@nexora.example. Examples include clicking a phishing link, sending Client Data to the wrong recipient, losing a device, noticing unusual system behaviour, or finding a colleague's password written down.
12.2 What not to do. Employees do not try to investigate an incident themselves, delete evidence, contact the suspected source, or discuss the incident outside those who need to know. They follow the SOC's instructions, which may include disconnecting a device from the network without switching it off.
12.3 Reporting to authorities and clients. The SOC assesses each incident, and the Company reports specified cyber security incidents to CERT-In within six hours of noticing them, as directed under the Information Technology Act, 2000. Clients are notified of incidents affecting their data within the time required by the contract.
12.4 No blame for honest reporting. An Employee who reports an incident promptly, including one caused by the Employee's own honest mistake, is not disciplined for the mistake. Concealing an incident, or delaying a report, is misconduct under the Code of Conduct and Ethics (NTL/HR/POL/004).

CCTV is used in common areas of offices, and never in washrooms, changing rooms, lactation rooms or rest rooms.
13.2 Limits. Monitoring is proportionate and automated. The content of an individual Employee's e-mail, chat or files is reviewed only for a specific investigation of a Security Incident or misconduct, with the written approval of the CISO and the Chief People Officer, and the review is logged. Personal apps and data on a BYOD Device are never monitored.
13.3 Use of monitoring data. Monitoring data is used only for security, compliance and investigations. It is not used to measure productivity or to rank Employees.

14. SOFTWARE, CLOUD SERVICES AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGY
14.1 Approved software. Only software in the approved software catalogue, available from the software centre on the Company laptop, may be installed. A request for new software is reviewed by Information Security for licensing and security within ten Working Days.
14.2 Cloud services. A cloud service, including any website or application that stores or processes Company or Client Data, may be used for work only if it is in the approved catalogue. Any other cloud service is prohibited for Company or Client Data, even if it is free, and even for a trial.
14.3 Open-source software. Open-source components in Company or client software are used only under licences approved by the Legal department, and are recorded in the project's software bill of materials. Components with known critical vulnerabilities are not used.

text:
15. PHYSICAL SECURITY
15.1 Access to premises. Employees badge in individually at every access point and do not allow others to follow them through a controlled door. Visitors are registered at reception, wear a visitor badge and are escorted at all times.
15.2 Clean desk. At the end of the day, and when leaving the desk for an extended period, Employees clear Confidential and Restricted documents from the desk, lock the screen, and lock away devices. Whiteboards in meeting rooms are wiped after client discussions.
15.3 Disposal. Paper containing Confidential or Restricted information is placed in the locked shredding bins. Devices and storage media are returned to the IT Service Desk for certified destruction and are never sold, given away or disposed of by the Employee.

title: IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
17. SECURE DEVELOPMENT
17.1 Secure coding. Employees who write code for the Company or its clients follow the secure coding standard published by Information Security, which addresses input validation, authentication, session management, error handling and the protection of secrets. Code is reviewed by a second developer before it is merged into a release branch.
17.2 Secrets in code. Passwords, API keys, tokens and certificates are never written into source code, configuration files committed to a repository, tickets or chat. They are stored in the approved secrets vault. Automated scanning checks every repository for secrets, and any secret found is treated as compromised and rotated immediately.
17.3 Repositories. Company and Client source code is stored only in repositories approved for the project. Copying code to a personal repository, a public code-hosting account or a personal device is prohibited, including code written by the Employee.
17.4 Testing and vulnerabilities. Applications are tested for security vulnerabilities before release, as required by the project's security plan. Critical and high-severity vulnerabilities are fixed before release or accepted in writing by the client and the CISO with a remediation date.

text:
18. THIRD-PARTY ACCESS
18.1 Vendors and contractors. A vendor or contractor is given access to Company systems or data only under a contract that includes confidentiality, security and data protection obligations, after a security assessment by Information Security proportionate to the access requested.
18.2 Sponsorship. Every third-party account has an Employee sponsor, who approves the access, ensures that it is used only for the contracted work, and requests its removal when the work ends. Third-party accounts expire automatically after 90 days unless renewed by the sponsor.
18.3 Sharing Personal Data with vendors. Personal Data of Employees is shared with a vendor, such as an insurer or a background verification agency, only where needed for a stated purpose, under a contract that restricts the vendor's use of the data to that purpose and requires its deletion afterwards.

Identity and contact details; identity numbers needed for tax and provident fund; bank details; education and employment history and background verification results; performance, attendance, leave and payroll records; photographs for identity cards; system access and security logs; and, where the Employee provides them, medical documents, disability information and details of dependants for insurance.

To recruit and employ Employees; to pay salaries and meet tax, provident fund and other legal obligations; to provide insurance and benefits; to manage performance, leave and attendance; to protect Information Assets and premises; to meet client requirements such as background checks; and to handle grievances, complaints and legal proceedings.

text:
CIRCULAR NO. HR/CIR/2025/02
Circular No.: HR/CIR/2025/02
Date of Issue: 2025-02-10
Effective From: 2025-03-01
Subject: Revised password requirements
Amends: Clause 5.2
Issued By: Chief Information Security Officer
In line with current guidance that frequent forced changes lead to weaker passwords, with effect from 1 March 2025: (a) passwords are at least 14 characters long, and a passphrase of several words is encouraged; (b) the requirement to change passwords every 90 days under Clause 5.2 is withdrawn, and a password is changed only when there is any indication that it may have been compromised, or when the SOC requires it; and (c) passwords are checked automatically against lists of known breached passwords, which may not be used. All other requirements of Clause 5.2 and of MFA under Clause 5.3 continue to apply.

title: IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy
text:
CIRCULAR NO. HR/CIR/2025/13
Circular No.: HR/CIR/2025/13
Date of Issue: 2025-12-08
Effective From: 2025-12-15
Subject: Use of generative AI tools
Amends: Clause 14.2
Issued By: Chief Information Security Officer and Chief Technology Officer
This Circular clarifies how Clause 14.2 applies to generative AI tools, such as AI chat assistants and code assistants, with effect from 15 December 2025. (a) Company and Client Data classified as Internal, Confidential or Restricted must not be entered into any public or consumer generative AI tool, including free versions of AI chat assistants, whether through a Company or a personal device. (b) The Company's approved AI assistant, available from the software centre, may be used with Internal and Confidential Company information. IT, Information Security and Acceptable Use Policy v5.0 (NTL/HR/POL/009), Amendment Circular HR/CIR/2025/13 (Use of generative AI tools), effective 2025-12-15, amends 14.2:
CIRCULAR NO. HR/CIR/2025/13
Circular No.: HR/CIR/2025/13
Date of Issue: 2025-12-08
Effective From: 2025-12-15
Subject: Use of generative AI tools
Amends: Clause 14.2
Issued By: Chief Information Security Officer and Chief Technology Officer
This Circular clarifies how Clause 14.2 applies to generative AI tools, such as AI chat assistants and code assistants, with effect from 15 December 2025. (a) Company and Client Data classified as Internal, Confidential or Restricted must not be entered into any public or consumer generative AI tool, including free versions of AI chat assistants, whether through a Company or a personal device. (b) The Company's approved AI assistant, available from the software centre, may be used with Internal and Confidential Company information. It may be used with Client Data only where the client has approved its use in writing and the project's security plan records the approval. (c) Output from any AI tool is reviewed by the Employee for accuracy, security and licensing before use, and the Employee remains responsible for it. (d) Entering Client Data into an unapproved AI tool is treated as a disclosure of Client Data under Clause 16.3.
